<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>



</system-reminder>

## /home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c/planning-notes.md
# Planning notes for mission artifacts (orchestrator, 2026-10-22)

Read this before any other mission file. It records what the owner decided after `SPEC.md` v0.2 was
written, and the readiness facts the mission is built on. Where these notes and `SPEC.md` disagree,
these notes win (owner decisions after the spec); `SPEC.md` is amended as-built at the next
integration (RULES rule 8). Where these notes are silent, `SPEC.md` is the authority.

Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory`).
Mission branch: `mission/observatory-v1` (created from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`).
Owner: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`).

## Files to read for context (all in the repository)

- `SPEC.md` (v0.2): §2 mission setup, §3 milestones S, M0–M5 with named tests and acceptance
  commands, §4 versions, §5 architecture, §6 tests, §7 CI, §8 deliverables.
- `ai/RULES.md` (binding), `AGENTS.md` (operational summary), `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6
  (FR ids, lanes, §7 event kinds, §10 metrics, appendix A canonical event).
- `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md` and
  `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md` (measured facts, pasted numbers).
- `config/observatory.example.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
  `docs/decisions/*.md`.

## Owner decisions after SPEC v0.1 (2026-10-22), all binding

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is
   selected from the Droid version recorded in the **fixture header** (`droid --version`, 0.247.0
   at capture). Token usage, model, tags and child linkage are read from the sibling
   `<session-id>.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`,
   `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage`, `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`,
   `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`). Child sessions are sibling files linked by
   `session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`. JSONL `type` values seen: `message`,
   `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`, `session_start`; `modelId`,
   `apiProvider`, `reasoningEffort` sit on assistant messages. Decision file at S integration; SPEC
   §3 M0 / §5.2 amended as-built then.
2. **Keyring.** `keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 (feature `keychain`,
   `set_default_store`) instead of `keyring` 4.x (fails `cargo deny`). Keychain items are generic
   passwords with service `droid-observatory/<name>` and account = the login user (`dct`), not the
   item name. Items present: `droid-observatory/github-token`, `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
   Decision file at S integration.
3. **DMG** only in the CI `bundle` job; local builds produce `.app` (`bundle.targets: ["app"]`).
4. **Tauri evidence.** Validators treat the Tauri window as a smoke check (process alive, `Running`
   log line, WebKit connections to port 3141, System Events lists the app). The browser surface
   (`trunk serve --port 3141` driven by `agent-browser`) is the primary interactive surface. At each
   milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked, attached to
   the report.
5. **Concurrency limits** (now SPEC §5.8 v0.2): max 3 concurrent agent-browser sessions per
   `trunk serve` (1.34–1.54 GB RSS each); `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10
   cores); all cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `trunk serve` and
   `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns 3141; cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s,
   incremental 1.46–2.08 s; `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
6. **GitHub token** is a fine-grained **read-only** PAT (Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Actions,
   Commit statuses, Metadata; repos droid-observatory and artstudio). No Checks permission: read
   check results through Actions runs (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`) and commit
   statuses (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), never the check-runs API.
7. **M4 exit (supersedes SPEC §3 M4 acceptance "merge from the app").** Merge button is visible when
   the policy allows and checks are green; with the read-only token the app surfaces the 403 cleanly
   (clear message naming the PR, target and missing permission; no crash, no retry storm); the
   **owner** performs the merge (UI or API); the badge updates from the poll (`policy-merged` or
   `merged` as detected). The write-token question stays at the M3→M4 boundary.
8. **Throttling and caps.** At a Factory usage throttle (5-hour / 7-day / monthly limits) or at a
   milestone cap, the run pauses at the point reached, usage so far is written to
   `reports/usage/`, the stall flag goes up and the owner is asked. **No silent model or
   reasoning-effort downgrade, ever** (a change is a decision file, rule 19). The M0-boundary re-cap
   of M1–M5 from measured S and M0 usage stays.
9. **Backlog = `BACKLOG.md` only.** No GitHub issues, no `scripts/gen-backlog.sh`, no `backlog`
   label. SPEC §8 "hybrid backlog" item is withdrawn; decision file at S integration records this.
   `AGENTS.md` and RULES rule 14 wording to be aligned (rule 14 is the owner's file; proposed
   wording: "everything else goes to `BACKLOG.md` with its reason").
10. **Reasoning effort** is `high` for all three roles (SPEC §2, `.factory/settings.json`,
    AGENTS.md agree). Models: orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`,
    validators `claude-opus-5-5` (D-006).
11. **Pre-mission artifacts** were committed by the orchestrator on `mission/observatory-v1`
    (`2266d3e`): readiness reports, SPEC §5.8, AGENTS.md runtime limits, session log 25–26.

## Execution model inside the mission

- Workers and validators of milestone `<m>` (`s`, `m0`, `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`) work only in
  the worktree `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>`.
  A stable symlink `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current` points at
  the active milestone's worktree; `services.yaml` commands use it.
- The first feature of each milestone after S is an **integration feature** (skill
  `integration-worker`): it merges the previous milestone (`git merge --no-ff wt/<prev>` into
  `mission/observatory-v1`), runs `make check`, pushes, waits for `mission-checks` green, writes the
  shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`,
  `reports/usage|readiness|ci`), records the owner's unlocked-display screenshot path, removes the
  old worktree, creates the new worktree and repoints `current`, then returns to the orchestrator
  with the boundary report (the human answers only here, rule 15).
- Final M5 integration and the single PR `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` are done by the
  orchestrator after the M5 validators pass.
- Tests first (rule 1): a red test is committed before the code that makes it green; the scrutiny
  validator checks the red run exists in the worker log.
- Ports: 3141 for the UI dev server (one `trunk serve` at a time); 3142–3149 scratch. Off-limits:
  5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444–18451, anything already listening.
- Off-limits: `main`, ruleset `main-gate`, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision, other
  worktrees, `~/.cargo/config.toml`, keychain values (never printed), `~/.factory/sessions/` is
  read-only (fixtures are copies, committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean and a
  reviewer read them).

## Validation tools available

- `cargo test`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay|inspect|metrics`, `make check`,
  `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80`, `make replay-fixtures`.
- `agent-browser` 0.37.1 against `http://localhost:3141` (open, snapshot, click, fill, screenshot,
  console, errors; `--session <name>` isolates). No first-run download observed.
- `make app-dev` / `cargo tauri dev` smoke evidence (see decision 4); `screencapture -x` only when
  the display is unlocked.
- `gh` 2.102 (logged in as `dctellya`, admin), `gh api` for rulesets, runs, statuses, PRs.
- `curl` against the Grafana OTLP endpoint (header from keychain, parsed `name=value`).
- `sqlite3` for the store; `security find-generic-password -s <service>` without `-w` for keychain
  attributes.

# droid-observatory v1: S + M0–M5 from SPEC.md

# droid-observatory v1 mission

Builds the Tauri 2 + Leptos desktop app described in `SPEC.md` v0.2 (v0.1 approved by the owner on 2026-10-22; v0.2 adds only the §5.8 concurrency limits the owner ordered). The spec is the authority; this proposal restates it in the mission's terms and records the readiness decisions taken at the planning boundary. Where the proposal and the spec differ, the spec wins and the difference is a bug in this proposal.

## 1. Plan overview

Seven milestones in SPEC §3 order, each integrated into `mission/observatory-v1` (already created from `main` at `c8524c2`, pre-mission commit `2266d3e` holds the readiness reports, SPEC §5.8, AGENTS.md and session-log entries 25–26). One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end, opened by the orchestrator, merged by the owner when `gate` is green.

| Milestone | Delivers | Cap (USD-eq) |
|---|---|---|
| **S** walking skeleton | workspace `crates/observatory-core`, `crates/observatory-cli`, `apps/observatory-app`; canonical `Event` with `EventKind::Unknown`, `SourcePtr`, `mapping_version`; `observatory-cli replay` printing `unknown events: N`; empty nine-lane Tauri window; `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml`; `cargo machete` + `cargo llvm-cov` (reported) in `mission-branch.yml`; B-016 version check in `release.yml`; snapshot `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`; hybrid backlog (`gh` issues labelled `backlog`, `scripts/gen-backlog.sh`) at integration | 40 |
| **M0** capture and mapping | fixture `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` + `.children/` frozen from this mission's own sessions at S integration; `mapping::v1` to PRD §7 kinds; `unknown events: 0` hard gate; SQLite store with pointer index; `inspect <event-id>`; decision files (mapping v1, `--tag`/child-session/role findings, session schema, keyring); coverage gate 80 % enforced from here | 60 |
| **M1** board, replay, attach | nine-lane board, cards by lane, worker sub-lanes, filters, scrubber, unmapped tray, Details Timeline, agent panel; `notify` + poll attach within 1 s; B-006 scrub pass; mission library (FR-L4); **Leptos go/no-go** (≤3 rework sessions, clean Trunk build) | 150 |
| **M2** host | launch screen; spawn `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc`; `RpcSource`; pause/message/answer; live output per agent | 80 |
| **M3** intervention | every control a lane-7 event with human actor; stall flag + runbook prompt; `docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md` revised | 60 |
| **M4** branch, gate, fix loop | `GitSource`, `GitHubSource` behind `Forge`; PR/check/ruleset/attestation detection; merge policy and `policy-merged`; Merge button; fix cycle; demo branch pair `demo/base` + ruleset `demo-gate` + `demo-gate.yml` (label `demo:red`) | 120 |
| **M5** time, waste, cost | time-state engine, rework windows, overhead, waste causes, tokens/cost at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, budget meter, model comparison, export, Details tabs, lane-9 charts, Grafana OTLP export (≤182 series worst case); oracle test against the owner's `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` | 120 |

Total cap 630 USD-eq. At the M0 boundary the orchestrator proposes re-caps for M1–M5 from measured S and M0 usage. M0 is also the gate for detailed M1–M5 planning: M1–M5 features are decomposed coarsely now and refined at the M0 boundary from the frozen mapping, without changing their scope.

## 2. Expected functionality (acceptance per milestone)

Each milestone's named tests (SPEC §3 "Tests green"), acceptance commands and gate are the validation contract's source. Common exit for every milestone: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green on the push, zero blocking findings, SPEC §9/§10 rows, README/BACKLOG/decisions index updated, `reports/usage/<m>.md`, `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json`, `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md` added, no `unknown.event` on the capture when the milestone adds a source.

Highlights of what the validators must see:
- **S**: `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` ends with `unknown events: N` (N > 0 allowed); `make app-dev` opens nine named empty lanes; `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`.
- **M0**: `make replay-fixtures`; replay of the M0 fixture ends with `unknown events: 0`; `inspect` prints the exact raw line by pointer; roles resolve for orchestrator, worker, both validators; children attach to their parent.
- **M1**: board renders the M0 capture in `trunk serve --port 3141` (fixture via file picker) and in the Tauri window; a `droid exec --mission` started in a terminal appears on the board within 1 s; scrubber, filters, tray count = unknown count; mission library lists past captures.
- **M2**: a short hosted mission on a scratch directory inside the worktree; pause/message/answer reach the orchestrator; hosted and attached views agree on event count; child process reaped on window close.
- **M3**: each control emits one lane-7 event; stall flag after `[intervention].stall_threshold_min` of no active time, none under threshold.
- **M4**: `demo/red-1` PR with `demo:red` → check fails → card loops to lane 3 with cycle count 1 → label removed → check green → Merge visible → merge from the app → badge updates → branch deleted; all run ids and PR numbers pasted. Target branch read from config.
- **M5**: `observatory-cli metrics <m0 fixture> --csv` within tolerance (1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD) of the owner's reference CSV; series appear in the owner's Grafana stack with only the allowed labels; telemetry stays off without the keychain item and the UI says so.

## 3. Architecture (SPEC §5, with planning-boundary refinements)

- **`observatory-core`** (sync, no tokio): `model` (canonical `Event`, `EventKind` incl. `Unknown`, `SourcePtr::Jsonl { path, byte_offset, byte_len }`, `mapping_version` on every event, lanes, roles), `ingest` (`Source` trait; `JsonlSource` for session files reading the JSONL **and its sibling `<id>.settings.json`** for token usage, model, tags and child linkage via `session_start.callingSessionId`; `RpcSource` M2; `GitSource`, `GitHubSource` behind `Forge` M4), `mapping::v1` (selected by the Droid version recorded in the fixture header; `droid --version` 0.247.0 is the target), `store` (rusqlite bundled, pointer index, raw lines never copied), `metrics` (time states, windows, cost, series budget), `view` (card position, filters, scrubber view-models, unit-tested here), `control` (lane-7 semantics), `config` (every threshold from `config/observatory.example.toml`), `secrets` (`keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2, generic-password lookup by service `droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user; OTLP header value parsed as `name=value` on the first `=`; never logged).
- **`observatory-cli`**: `replay`, `inspect`, `metrics --csv` over core; exit codes and the `unknown events: N` line are the oracle the validators compare the UI against.
- **`apps/observatory-app`**: Tauri 2.12 shell (tokio only here: `rt-multi-thread, process, macros`) exposing commands over core; Leptos 0.8 CSR UI built by Trunk 0.22, no logic beyond rendering. Dev URL `http://localhost:3141`.
- **Telemetry**: `opentelemetry` 0.33 + `opentelemetry-otlp` (`http-proto`, `metrics`, `reqwest-blocking-client`) to Grafana Cloud behind `[telemetry].enabled`; label allow-list and the §5.7 budget enforced in core.
- **GitHub access**: fine-grained read-only PAT from the keychain (Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Actions, Commit statuses, Metadata). Check results are read via Actions runs and commit statuses, **not** the check-runs API (no Checks permission). Open point for the M3→M4 boundary: the Merge button needs write on Pull requests; with the current token the app must surface the 403 cleanly, and the owner decides whether to widen the token for the M4 demo.
- **Decision files due at S integration** (owner-approved today): keyring variant B; session schema (no Droid version in files → fixture header; usage in `.settings.json`; sibling child files); read-only PAT → Actions runs + statuses; hybrid backlog; coverage and machete (SPEC §8).

Full detail will be in `architecture.md` in the mission directory.

## 4. Environment setup

Already done and verified on 2026-10-22 (`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`): Rust 1.99.1 via `rust-toolchain.toml` (rustfmt, clippy, wasm32), trunk 0.22.0, tauri-cli 2.12.4, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 + llvm-tools-preview, cargo-machete 0.9.2, cargo-deny 0.20.2, gitleaks, markdownlint-cli2, lychee, actionlint, gh 2.102 (logged in as `dctellya`, admin on the repo), agent-browser 0.37.1, Droid 0.247.0. `make doctor` reports all ok. `make hooks` enabled; `.factory/hooks.json` guards git and logs tool calls.

`init.sh` will only re-run `make doctor` and `make hooks` and verify the worktree exists; nothing is installed per session. Machine quirks workers must know: global `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target` with `sccache`, so all cargo builds serialize on one lock; `[profile.dev] opt-level = 1` applies to wasm builds.

## 5. Infrastructure and boundaries

- **Branch/worktree policy (SPEC §2)**: workers and validators of milestone `<m>` work only in `../observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` (created by the orchestrator from `mission/observatory-v1` when the milestone starts). The orchestrator integrates with `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`, runs `make check`, pushes, waits for `mission-checks` green, writes the shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) and removes the worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file.
- **Git**: forward only; never amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push; never push to `main`; never `--no-verify`; commit subject ≤ 72 chars; trailer `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. Tests first: the red test is committed before the code.
- **Ports**: 3141 for the UI dev server (one `trunk serve` owns it at a time); 3142–3149 for scratch. Off-limits: 5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444–18451 and anything else already listening.
- **Off-limits**: `main` and its `main-gate` ruleset, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision file, other worktrees, `~/.cargo/config.toml`, the owner's Ollama/SurrealDB/Docker services, keychain values (read via the API, never printed), `~/.factory/sessions/` is read-only (snapshots are copies into `fixtures/`, committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean and a reviewer read them).
- **One outward write**: the demo-pair merge in M4 (from the app, human-confirmed) and the ruleset/branch/label setup for `demo/base` by the orchestrator with `gh`. Nothing else leaves the machine except pushes of `mission/**`, `wt/**`, `demo/**` branches and the final PR.
- **Secrets**: keychain `droid-observatory/github-token` and `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` (both present), `GITHUB_TOKEN` env as fallback for the token only.

## 6. Testing strategy (SPEC §6)

Gate command everywhere: `make check` (markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers, decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, `cargo machete`, `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` from M0). Suites: unit tests next to code; fixture replay + golden mapping tests in `crates/observatory-core/tests/`; attach latency harness; CLI tests; metrics oracle (M5); telemetry budget (M5). UI logic is unit-tested in core; no wasm test runner. Scrutiny validators check that each feature's red test run exists in the worker log (rule 1). CI: `mission-branch.yml` aggregate `mission-checks` (budget 3 min warm, wall time pasted to `reports/ci/`), `demo-gate.yml` (M4), `gate.yml` on the final PR.

## 7. User testing strategy

Verified executable on 2026-10-22 (`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`):
- **Browser surface (primary)**: `trunk serve --config <ui Trunk.toml> --port 3141 --open false` (55.9 s cold, 1.5–2.1 s incremental); validators drive it with `agent-browser` (open, snapshot, click, screenshot, console/errors), isolated per `--session`. Fixtures are opened through the file picker. Evidence: screenshots, snapshot refs, console errors, CLI output as oracle.
- **Tauri surface (smoke check)**: `make app-dev` (37.7 s to running app). agent-browser cannot attach to WKWebView; evidence is process alive, `Running` log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing, plus `screencapture` when the display is unlocked. At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked and it is attached to the report (owner decision).
- **Live attach/host**: a `droid exec --mission` on a scratch directory inside the worktree, with timestamps from the attach-latency test and validator clocks.
- **Concurrency (SPEC §5.8 v0.2)**: at most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (~1.5 GB RSS each); `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores); cargo builds serialize on the shared target lock; `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when one trunk owns 3141. Validators run user tests only after builds finish.

## 8. Mission readiness

- Toolchain and crates verified (§4 above); Tauri 2 + Leptos CSR scaffold builds and runs; DMG bundling only in the CI `bundle` job (fails non-interactively locally).
- Grafana OTLP endpoint answers 200 with the parsed keychain header.
- GitHub rulesets and Actions APIs answer under the owner's `gh` auth; `main-gate` ruleset present; the token can create `demo-gate`.
- Session file schema inspected (14 JSONL files in the mission's sessions dir at check time); the capture plan (B-010) is feasible from this mission's own sessions.
- Validation path executable end to end: `make check` exit 0 on the mission branch; agent-browser drove the scaffold on 3141 with zero console errors.
- Human inputs still scheduled (SPEC §2): M1 go/no-go, M0-boundary re-caps, M3→M4 token write permission question, M4→M5 reference CSV, final PR merge. Model ids per `.factory/settings.json` (orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`, all `high`).

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- Attach-to-render latency < 1 s per event; `mission-checks` warm < 3 min; `observatory-core` line coverage ≥ 80 % from M0; telemetry series ≤ 182 worst case (< 200); no `unknown.event` dropped, count always visible; raw lines read-only, never uploaded or copied into the store; secrets only from keychain/env, never in repo, store or logs; every threshold in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason; every count/timing pasted from a tool; files > 200 KB only under `fixtures/streams/` and `build-log/`; `cargo deny` clean on every dependency; budget caps per milestone with the stall flag at a cap.

# droid-observatory architecture

Authoritative design for the mission `observatory-v1`. Written for implementation workers (Rust,
Leptos, Tauri, CI) who will not read the PRD. Sources, in precedence order: `planning-notes.md`
(owner decisions after the spec, binding), `SPEC.md` v0.2, `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6,
`docs/decisions/D-*`, the two readiness reports of 2026-10-22, `config/observatory.example.toml`.
Where the sources leave a choice, the choice here is marked `[arch decision]` with its reason.
Paths are relative to the repository root unless absolute. Numbers are pasted from the readiness
reports; none are estimated.

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SourceKind { Jsonl, Rpc, Git, GitHub }

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.
    /// Never blocks longer than one poll interval; never returns an error for "no data".
    fn next_batch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>, IngestError>;
    /// True when every known file has been read to its current end (replay = attach that reached EOF, D-008).
    fn at_eof(&self) -> bool;
}
```

`[arch decision]` `next_batch` + `at_eof` replace SPEC §5.4's `poll`: the name says it pulls, and
`at_eof` is what makes replay and attach one code path (the CLI stops at `at_eof()`, the watcher keeps
calling). `IngestError` (thiserror): `Io { path, source }`, `FileMoved { path }`, `TooLarge { path, mb }`.

### 4.2 JsonlSource (S; sidecar and children M0)

```rust
pub struct JsonlSource { /* files: Vec<TailState { path, session_id, offset: u64, partial: Vec<u8> }>, cfg: IngestConfig */ }
impl JsonlSource {
    pub fn open(root: &Path, cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;   // root = the orchestrator .jsonl
    pub fn add_file(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<SessionId, IngestError>;   // child or newly discovered file
    pub fn read_at(path: &Path, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IngestError>; // used by inspect/Details
}
```

Reading rules: open read-only; read from `offset` in chunks of `tail_chunk_kb`; split on `\n`; an
incomplete trailing fragment stays in `partial` until the newline arrives (a writer may be mid-line);
`byte_offset` is the offset of the first byte of the line, `byte_len` excludes the newline; a line
that is not valid JSON is still a `RawRecord` (mapping yields `Unknown { raw_type: "<unparseable>" }`).
Files over `max_session_file_mb` are indexed and a `TooLarge` warning is surfaced once.

### 4.3 Watcher (M1, feature `watch`)

```rust
pub struct SessionWatcher { /* notify::RecommendedWatcher + poll fallback */ }
impl SessionWatcher {
    pub fn start(cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;  // scans cfg.factory_sessions_dir recursively
    pub fn next_discovered(&mut self) -> Vec<DiscoveredSession>;    // new *.jsonl since last call (notify or poll)
}
pub struct DiscoveredSession { pub path: PathBuf, pub session_id: SessionId, pub parent: Option<SessionId>,
                               pub name: String /* first tag, else session id (FR-L1) */ }
```

Design: `notify` 8.2.0 (FSEvents) for create/modify; a poll every `jsonl_poll_ms` (500) re-stats every
watched file and lists the directory, because FSEvents coalesces and a file created before start would be
missed (PRD §14). Startup scan attaches files modified in the last 24 h as growing [arch decision: a
bound so a directory with hundreds of old sessions does not open them all; older files stay in the
library and open on demand]. At most `max_watched_sessions` (64) files are tailed, newest first; the
UI shows "N sessions not watched". Growth is read by `JsonlSource::next_batch` in one `tail_chunk_kb`
step per poll. Everything runs on one `std::thread` owned by the shell (`backend.rs`), which batches
events toward the UI every `event_batch_ms` (100).

### 4.4 Capture header for live attach

`captures` row per attached directory: `id`, `source_dir`, `droid_version`, `started_at`. No file is
written next to Droid's files.

#!/bin/sh
# Factory PreToolUse hook: the write guard (ai/RULES.md rules 12 and 13).
# Blocks history rewrites and direct pushes to main from any agent. Exit 2 = block.
set -u
input=$(cat)
cmd=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty')
[ -n "$cmd" ] || exit 0

deny() { echo "blocked by .factory/hooks/guard-git.sh: $1 (ai/RULES.md rule 12: git forward only)" >&2; exit 2; }

printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -Eq 'git[[:space:]]+(commit[^|;&]*--amend|reset[[:space:]]+--(hard|soft|mixed)|rebase|stash|push[^|;&]*(--force|-f\b|\+))' && deny "history rewrite"
printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -Eq 'git[[:space:]]+push[^|;&]*[[:space:]](origin[[:space:]]+)?(HEAD:)?main\b' && deny "direct push to main"
printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -Eq 'git[[:space:]]+(checkout|switch)[[:space:]]+main\b' && printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -Eq 'git[[:space:]]+commit' && deny "committing on main"
exit 0

#!/bin/sh
# Factory PostToolUse hook: append one compact JSON line per tool call to build-log/
# (ai/RULES.md rule 17). Records what was called, never the tool response, so the
# log stays small and cannot leak tool output.
set -u
input=$(cat)
root=${FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR:-$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.cwd')}
day=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
dir="$root/build-log/$day"
mkdir -p "$dir"
session=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.session_id // "unknown"')
printf '%s' "$input" | jq -c --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '{
  ts: $ts,
  session_id: .session_id,
  event: .hook_event_name,
  tool: .tool_name,
  command: (.tool_input.command // null),
  file: (.tool_input.file_path // null),
  summary: (.tool_input.summary // null),
  exit_code: (.tool_response.exitCode // null)
}' >> "$dir/$session.jsonl"
exit 0

#!/bin/sh
# Pre-push: refuse history rewrites and direct pushes to main (ai/RULES.md rule 12).
set -eu
remote=$1
while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  case "$remote_ref" in
    refs/heads/main)
      echo "pre-push: direct push to main refused; open the mission's pull request instead"
      exit 1 ;;
  esac
  # A non-fast-forward push means history was rewritten.
  if [ "$remote_sha" != "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] && [ "$local_sha" != "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
    if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote_sha" "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "pre-push: $remote_ref is not a fast-forward; history rewrites are forbidden (rule 12)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
done
exit 0

Practical Tauri validation evidence, in order of strength:

1. Same UI validated in Chromium through trunk serve on 3141 (functional evidence; the Tauri shell
   loads the identical `devUrl`).
2. `cargo tauri dev` log contains `Running .../debug/<crate>` with no panic afterwards, and the
   process stays alive (`ps -p <pid>`; measured RSS 130 MB).
3. `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` shows `com.apple.WebKit` ESTABLISHED connections to trunk (the webview
   fetched the page).
4. System Events lists the process with `background only is false` and `visible true`; with the
   screen unlocked, `count windows` should be 1 and `name of windows` the configured title.
5. `screencapture -x` of the screen (unlocked only); window-only capture needs the CGWindow id,
   which this machine's `python3` cannot obtain (`No module named 'Quartz'`); use Swift or JXA.
6. For true in-window interaction, the mission would need a tauri-driver/WebDriver setup, which is
   out of scope here and not supported by tauri-driver on macOS at the moment of writing.

Shutdown gotcha: `kill <cargo-tauri pid>` left `trunk serve` and the app binary running,
reparented to PID 1:

```text
--- after kill 86056 (cargo-tauri)
86173     1 trunk serve --config ui/Trunk.toml
86243     1 /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target/debug/src-tauri
```

Both had to be killed by PID. Kill the whole process group (`kill -- -<pgid>`) or kill the three
PIDs. After that: no `cargo-tauri`/`trunk`/`src-tauri` processes, `lsof 3141` exit 1, System Events
no longer lists `src-tauri`.

## Concurrency and cost

Measured surfaces (RSS and CPU from ps, build times from cargo output):

| Surface | Startup | Steady state | Build burst | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trunk serve` (dev wasm, cold) | 55.9 s to first HTTP 200 | 35 MB RSS, 0.1 %CPU | up to 7 rustc at 40-99 %CPU each, largest rustc 727 MB RSS | medium during build, low idle |
| `trunk serve` incremental rebuild | 1.5-2.1 s | same | 1-2 rustc | low |
| agent-browser session (Chrome, headless) | 1.25-1.44 s | 1.34-1.54 GB summed RSS (11-12 procs), 0-1 %CPU idle | 40 %CPU browser + 25 %CPU GPU helper for ~2 s at launch | medium (memory), low (CPU) |
| `cargo tauri dev` (native, warm wasm) | 37.7 s to app process (31.2 s cargo build) | app 130 MB RSS, 0.0 %CPU; trunk child 35 MB | native rustc burst, serialized after trunk's build | medium during build, low idle |
| `cargo test` (core-deps scratch, warm) | 2.6 s | - | - | low when warm |
| `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` (core-deps, separate `llvm-cov-target` dir) | 44.3 s | - | peak 7 rustc, 1.27 GB summed rustc RSS, sum 396 %CPU; load 1-min went 3.3 -> 14.6 | high |

Lock behaviour observed:

- trunk rebuild concurrent with a native `cargo build` in another crate: both logged
  `Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache`, trunk additionally logged
  `Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`. They serialize; neither failed.
- `cargo llvm-cov` builds under `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/llvm-cov-target`, so it did not block on the
  build-directory lock held by trunk (0 `Blocking` lines in its log) and only shares the brief
  package-cache lock. It does compete for CPU: the load average hit 14.6 on 10 cores.
- Running `cargo tauri dev` already serializes internally: trunk's wasm build takes the lock first,
  then `cargo run` for the native crate.

70 % headroom rule (use at most 7 cores and 44.8 GB; baseline load 3-6 and about 60 % memory
free per `memory_pressure`, i.e. about 38 GB usable):

- (a) Concurrent agent-browser validator subagents against one trunk serve: **3**. Each session is
  about 1.5 GB RSS upper bound and near-zero idle CPU, so memory allows more, but each validator
  also runs an LLM-driven CLI loop and the page is a single shared dev server with a live-reload
  websocket; three keeps total browser memory under 5 GB and leaves CPU for one build. Use
  `--session <name>` per validator; sessions are isolated (verified above). Do not exceed 5.
- (b) `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexisting: **yes, but run one trunk only**. `cargo tauri
  dev` starts its own `trunk serve` on 3141 via `beforeDevCommand`; a separately started trunk on
  3141 would make the second one fail to bind. Either run only `cargo tauri dev` (its trunk serves
  the browser validators too, verified: `curl` on 3141 answered while the Tauri window was up) or
  point the standalone trunk at a scratch port 3142-3149. Compiles serialize on the shared target
  lock; expect the native build (31 s warm deps) to wait for any in-flight wasm build.
- (c) `cargo test`, `cargo llvm-cov`, `trunk serve` at the same time: **technically possible,
  recommend serializing llvm-cov**. `cargo test` and trunk share the build-directory lock and
  serialize automatically (safe, just slower). `cargo llvm-cov` uses its own target dir, so it runs
  truly in parallel and pushed the 1-min load from 3.3 to 14.6 on 10 cores, above the 7-core
  budget. Run llvm-cov alone (or only with idle servers), and let `cargo test` and trunk rebuilds
  serialize on the lock.

Memory check: at the peak of the concurrent test (7 rustc, 1.27 GB) plus two Chrome sessions
(about 2.9 GB) plus the Tauri app (130 MB), `memory_pressure` still reported 60 % free. Memory is
not the constraint on this machine; CPU and the shared target lock are.

## Gotchas

- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target` comes from the shell environment, not
  from `~/.cargo/config.toml`. All cargo-driven builds (trunk, tauri, test) share one build
  directory lock and log `Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory` when they collide.
  `cargo llvm-cov` is the exception (own `llvm-cov-target` subdir).
- `~/.cargo/config.toml` sets `[profile.dev] opt-level = 1, debug = 1` globally; the dev wasm
  build is therefore `[optimized + debuginfo]`, not a plain debug build. The mission's own profile
  settings in Cargo.toml will be merged with this.
- sccache is the rustc wrapper; its Rust hit rate during this session was 0.30 % (`Cache hits
  (Rust) 6`, `Cache misses (Rust) 1993`), so it gives no speedup for fresh dependency sets yet.
- Trunk flags: `--open false` (not `--open=false`), `--config ui/Trunk.toml` when the Trunk.toml is
  not in the cwd. Trunk 0.22.0 prints a `starting build` line and `success` when ready; the
  `server listening at` block also lists every `/etc/hosts`-style name (CRC OpenShift entries
  here), which is noise.
- Dev page HTML contains trunk's live-reload script (websocket to `/.well-known/trunk/ws`); a
  validator that reads the raw HTML must look at `<main>`, not the top of `<body>`. `snapshot`
  already does this.
- agent-browser: no first-run download (`agent-browser doctor` found Google Chrome 155 at
  `/Applications` and reported `Headless launch + about:blank in 1.45s`). State lives in
  `~/.agent-browser/` (36 KB). A daemon lingers per session (default idle timeout 1 h); use
  `agent-browser close --all` at the end of a validation. A failed `connect` still leaves a
  `tauri` daemon entry; close it too. `agent-browser doctor` prints `No encryption key set`
  (informational, only relevant for `auth save`).
- `cargo tauri dev` process tree: killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans `trunk serve` and the app
  binary (both reparent to PID 1 and keep running, trunk keeps 3141 bound). Kill all three PIDs or
  the process group.
- The debug app binary is `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/<crate-name>` (`src-tauri` here); match the
  process by that path, and note the `productName` only affects the bundle, not the dev binary.
- Screen lock: this run happened with the screen locked (`CGSSessionScreenIsLocked true`), so
  `screencapture -x` produced a black 4112x2658 image (luma 16 everywhere) and System Events
  reported 0 windows for the app. No permission prompt appeared; Accessibility is already trusted
  for the iTerm2 chain (`AXIsProcessTrusted() true`). Validators that need a Tauri screenshot
  require an unlocked, logged-in display; schedule those steps accordingly or accept
  process/log/System-Events evidence instead.
- `python3` on PATH has no `Quartz` (pyobjc) module, so CGWindowList enumeration must use JXA or
  Swift if a window-only capture (`screencapture -l <windowid>`) is wanted.
- `top` is rejected by the agent runtime as interactive; sample with
  `ps -axo pid,ppid,rss,%cpu,command` and `sysctl -n vm.loadavg`. `ps` prints decimal commas
  (`43,0`) in this locale; convert before summing.
- Timing numbers: cold dev wasm build 53.64 s (190 crates); warm native Tauri build 31.18 s;
  incremental wasm rebuild 1.46-2.08 s; agent-browser open 1.25-1.44 s; llvm-cov on a 14-dep
  scratch crate 44.3 s; trunk ready-to-curl 55.94 s; tauri launch-to-app-process 37.66 s.

# Release

**When:** the mission PR has merged into `main` and the human decides the result is a
release (D-009). Agents do not push tags.

## Steps

```sh
git switch main && git pull --ff-only
git tag -a v<MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH> -m "v<MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH>"
git push origin v<MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH>
gh run watch                         # workflow: release
gh release view v<MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH>
```

`release.yml` refuses a tag that is not on `main` or not semver. With the Tauri app present
it attaches the signed `.dmg` and its sigstore bundle; before that, the release has notes
only.

## If it fails

- `verify` failed: the tag is on the wrong commit. Do not move the tag; push a new patch tag
  from the right commit and delete the GitHub release draft if one exists.
- `bundle` failed: same fix path as the gate's `bundle` job ([red-gate.md](red-gate.md)).
- Notes are wrong: they come from PR titles and labels (`.github/release.yml`); edit the
  release text on GitHub and fix the label for next time.

# Fix cycle

**Symptom:** the mission has ended (orchestrator reported `mission.completed`) but CI on the
mission PR is red, or a check turned red after a rerun.

The fix is a new cycle on the **same branch and the same PR** (PRD §2, D-001). Nothing is
reopened on `main`.

## Steps

1. Label the PR `fix-cycle`. Read the failing job output (see [red-gate.md](red-gate.md)).
2. Write the fix mission file: the affected feature's spec section, the failing check output
   pasted verbatim, the mission branch name, and the original session ids
   (`~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`). The observatory pre-fills this from M4 onward; until
   then copy it by hand.
3. Start the fix in the repository checkout on the mission branch:

   ```sh
   git switch mission/<name>
   droid exec --mission --auto high \
     --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
     --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort high \
     --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
     --output-format text \
     -f fix-<name>.md
   ```

4. The fix commits land on the mission branch as new commits; the PR updates; the gate
   reruns. Record the cycle in the session log and in `reports/` (time and tokens pasted
   from the tool).
5. Merge only when `gate` is green, by the human.

## Stop and involve the human when

- The failure is in a required check that does not belong to this repository (GitHub
  outage, action removed upstream).
- The fix would change the spec: propose it with reason and cost first (rule 9).

# Stalled mission

**Symptom:** a feature shows no active time for longer than
`[intervention].stall_threshold_min` (default 20 minutes, `config/observatory.example.toml`),
or the orchestrator has been waiting on a question nobody saw.

## Confirm

Until M1 (attach): tail the orchestrator session file and look at the last event's timestamp.

```sh
ls -t ~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/*.jsonl | head -1 | xargs tail -n 3
```

From M1 the board shows the stall flag on the card; from M3 the card offers suggested
prompts.

## Causes and actions

| Last event seen | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `question.asked` / `permission.requested` | Waiting on human | Answer in the terminal that runs the mission (M2 hosting: in the app) |
| `subagent.spawned` with no child file growing | Worker died or is blocked on a tool | Check the child session file; if silent, send a message to the orchestrator to retry or skip the task |
| `hook.blocked` repeated | An agent keeps hitting `guard-git.sh` or a git hook | Read `build-log/<day>/<session>.jsonl` for the command; the agent needs the forward-only instruction, not a bypass |
| `integration.conflict` | Two worktrees touched one file (rule 13 violated) | Orchestrator resolves at integration; if it loops, stop and split ownership in the spec |
| Nothing for a long time, process alive | Long tool call (build, tests) | Wait one more threshold; then `mission.paused` and inspect |

## Stop and involve the human when

- The suggested action is to change scope, model or threshold (decision file).
- The stall repeats on the same feature after one retry.

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/docs/runbooks/hooks-disabled.md
# Hooks disabled

**Symptom:** a commit landed without the pre-commit output, a push to `main` was attempted,
`build-log/` has no line for a tool call, or an agent amended or rebased.

Two hook sets protect rule 12 and rule 17:

| Set | Where | Enabled by | Enforces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Git hooks | `.githooks/` | `make hooks` (sets `core.hooksPath`) | pre-commit checks, 72-char subject, no push to `main`, no non-fast-forward |
| Factory hooks | `.factory/hooks.json` | present in the checkout | `guard-git.sh` blocks amend/reset/rebase/stash/force/push-to-main (exit 2); `log-tool-call.sh` writes `build-log/` |

## Confirm

```sh
git config core.hooksPath            # must print .githooks
ls .githooks && test -x .githooks/pre-commit
jq . .factory/hooks.json             # both hooks listed
ls build-log/$(date +%F)/            # one file per session today
```

## Fix

- `core.hooksPath` empty or wrong: `make hooks`. Each worktree is its own checkout; run it
  there too.
- Hook files not executable: `chmod +x .githooks/* .factory/hooks/*.sh` and commit.
- `build-log/` silent: `jq` missing (`make doctor`), or the session runs outside the repo
  root. The hook needs the repository as the working directory.
- History was rewritten anyway: do not "fix" by rewriting again. Push the current state
  forward as new commits and record what happened in the session log and `reports/`.

## Stop and involve the human when

- A hook was edited or deleted by an agent: that is a rule 12 breach, logged and reviewed
  before anything else continues.
- `main` received a direct push (the ruleset should make this impossible; if it happened,
  the ruleset changed, which is a decision).

# Red gate

**Symptom:** the `gate` check on the pull request into `main` is red, so the ruleset blocks
the merge.

## Confirm

```sh
gh pr checks <pr> --watch=false
gh run view <run-id> --log-failed
```

`gate` is an aggregate; the failing job is one of `light / *`, `sast`, `sast-upload`,
`fs-scan`, `workflow-policy`, `sbom`, `bundle`.

## Fix by job

| Job | Local reproduction | Typical cause |
|---|---|---|
| `light / docs` | `make check-docs check-file-size check-todos check-decisions-index` | markdownlint, stale decisions index, bare `TODO` |
| `light / links` | `make check-links` | dead URL; if the site is flaky, add it to `lychee.toml` `exclude` with a comment |
| `light / workflows` | `make check-workflows` | actionlint |
| `light / secrets` | `make check-secrets` | a leaked value: rotate it first, then remove it with a new commit (never rewrite history, rule 12) |
| `light / rust`, `light / deny` | `make fmt-check lint test deny` | warnings are errors; a new dependency fails `deny` until its licence or advisory is handled |
| `sast` | run the container: `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src" semgrep/semgrep:<version> semgrep scan --config p/default --config p/rust --error` | findings show on the PR via code scanning; fix or add an inline `nosemgrep` with a reason |
| `fs-scan` | `trivy fs --severity HIGH,CRITICAL .` | vulnerable dependency or misconfiguration; findings also in the Security tab |
| `workflow-policy` | `checkov -d .github/workflows --framework github_actions` | unpinned action, missing permissions block |
| `bundle` | `make app-build` on macOS | Trunk or Tauri toolchain; see D-002 go/no-go if it recurs |

Push the fix as a new commit on the mission branch. The gate reruns on the PR.

## Stop and involve the human when

- The fix needs a change to `rust-toolchain.toml`, a workflow permission, or the ruleset
  (each is a decision file).
- `secrets` found a real credential (rotation is the owner's).
- The same job has failed three times on the same cause (rule 15 stall).

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
# Light checks on mission branches (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 11).
# Target: under three minutes warm. Independent jobs run in parallel; the
# aggregate job `mission-checks` is the single name other tooling depends on.
#
# Rust jobs activate automatically once Cargo.toml exists (walking skeleton).

name: mission-branch

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: mission-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  docs:
    name: docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: markdownlint
        uses: DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2-action@21c1be1b93ad9ed58fa840aacc3f279cde2a72ff # v24.2.0
        with:
          globs: "**/*.md"
      - name: decisions index is current
        run: make check-decisions-index
      - name: file size
        run: make check-file-size
      - name: debt markers reference an issue or backlog item
        run: make check-todos

  links:
    name: links
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@e7477775783ea5526144ba13e8db5eec57747ce8 # v2.9.0
        with:
          args: --config lychee.toml --no-progress "**/*.md"
          fail: true

  workflows:
    name: workflows
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: actionlint
        uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
        with:
          args: -color

  secrets:
    name: secrets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@e0c47f4f8be36e29cdc102c57e68cb5cbf0e8d1e # v3.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  rust:
    name: rust
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable; version from rust-toolchain.toml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - name: fmt
        run: make fmt-check
      - name: clippy
        run: make lint
      - name: test
        run: make test
      - name: replay fixtures
        if: needs.detect.outputs.has_fixtures == 'true'
        run: make replay-fixtures

  deny:
    name: deny
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@3c6349835b2b7b196a839186cb8b78e02f7b5f25 # v2.1.1
        with:
          command: check
          arguments: --all-features

  mission-checks:
    name: mission-checks
    needs: [detect, docs, links, workflows, secrets, rust, deny]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - name: aggregate
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: |
          echo "$RESULTS"
          if echo "$RESULTS" | grep -Eq '"result": *"(failure|cancelled)"'; then
            echo "a required job failed"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "all mission-branch checks passed or were not applicable"

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/.github/workflows/gate.yml
# The gate: the mission's single pull request into main (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 12).
# Everything from mission-branch.yml plus SAST, filesystem scan, workflow policy,
# SBOM, the macOS Tauri bundle (bundle.yml), build provenance and cosign signatures.
# Semgrep and Trivy results are uploaded as SARIF to GitHub code scanning so
# findings appear on the PR and in the Security tab (BACKLOG B-013).
# It never deploys.
#
# `gate` is the aggregate job and the only required status check in the main
# ruleset (docs/decisions/D-003). Add jobs by appending them to its `needs`.

name: gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: gate-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
      has_tauri: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_tauri }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if [ -f apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json ]; then echo "has_tauri=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_tauri=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  light:
    name: light
    uses: ./.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read

  sast:
    name: sast
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    container:
      image: semgrep/semgrep:1.182.0
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: semgrep
        run: semgrep scan --config p/default --config p/rust --config p/secrets --config p/github-actions --error --metrics=off --sarif --output semgrep.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: semgrep-results
          path: semgrep.sarif

  # Separate job: the codeql-action needs the runner's Node, which the semgrep
  # container does not provide.
  sast-upload:
    name: sast-upload
    needs: sast
    if: always() && needs.sast.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: semgrep-results
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        with:
          sarif_file: semgrep.sarif
          category: semgrep

  fs-scan:
    name: fs-scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: trivy filesystem scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25 # v0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: .
          scanners: vuln,misconfig,secret
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          exit-code: "1"
          ignore-unfixed: true
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: trivy-results
          path: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
          category: trivy

  workflow-policy:
    name: workflow-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: checkov on the workflows themselves
        uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@c3e106d5f8f4253a6de5110efb41a080f83db294 # v12
        with:
          directory: .github/workflows
          framework: github_actions
          soft_fail: false

  sbom:
    name: sbom
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c # v0.24.3
        with:
          path: .
          format: spdx-json
          artifact-name: sbom.spdx.json
          upload-artifact: true

  bundle:
    name: bundle
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_tauri == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/bundle.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write

  gate:
    name: gate
    needs: [detect, light, sast, sast-upload, fs-scan, workflow-policy, sbom, bundle]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - name: aggregate
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: |
          echo "$RESULTS"
          if echo "$RESULTS" | grep -Eq '"result": *"(failure|cancelled)"'; then
            echo "a gate job failed"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "gate green"

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/.github/workflows/bundle.yml
# Reusable: the macOS Tauri bundle with build provenance and a keyless cosign
# signature. Called by gate.yml (every PR into main) and release.yml (tags), so
# the artifact a release ships is built by the same steps the gate checked.
# Callers decide whether to run it (they probe for the Tauri config first).

name: bundle

on:
  workflow_call:
    outputs:
      artifact:
        description: Name of the uploaded bundle artifact
        value: ${{ jobs.bundle.outputs.artifact }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  bundle:
    name: bundle
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    outputs:
      artifact: bundle-macos
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable; version from rust-toolchain.toml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@a4d3f3f761dcd95cce1b72cb61cb6d1963438177 # v2.87.30
        with:
          tool: trunk,tauri-cli
      - name: build bundle
        run: make app-build
      - name: attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: |
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - name: cosign sign (keyless)
        run: |
          for f in target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg; do
            cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle "$f.sigstore.json" "$f"
          done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-macos
          path: |
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.sigstore.json

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/.github/workflows/release.yml
# Release: a tag v* pushed to a commit that is on main (docs/decisions/D-009).
# Builds the bundle with the same reusable workflow the gate used, then creates
# the GitHub release with notes generated from the merged PR's labels
# (.github/release.yml). Nothing here deploys anywhere else.

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    outputs:
      has_tauri: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_tauri }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: tag points at a commit on main
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main; then
            echo "tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} is not on main; releases come only from main"; exit 1
          fi
      - name: tag is semver
        run: |
          echo "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$' \
            || { echo "tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} is not vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"; exit 1; }
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json ]; then echo "has_tauri=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_tauri=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  bundle:
    name: bundle
    needs: verify
    if: needs.verify.outputs.has_tauri == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/bundle.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write

  release:
    name: release
    needs: [verify, bundle]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.bundle.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.bundle.result == 'success'
        with:
          name: bundle-macos
          path: dist/release
      - name: create release with generated notes
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          files=""
          if [ -d dist/release ]; then files=$(find dist/release -type f | tr '\n' ' '); fi
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$TAG" $files

# Price table used to turn tokens into money when the stream does not report credits
# (PRD §10.5). Dated: every cost shown by the observatory names the table it used.
#
# Prices are per million tokens, USD, standard (non-batch) API rates, 5-minute cache writes.

effective = "2026-10-22"
currency = "USD"
source = "https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing"

# D-007: Ruleset on main

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

`main` is the gate the observatory watches. Its rules must be the ones the PRD's merge
policy reader (FR-G4) will find, and they must not hang the final PR.

## Decision

GitHub ruleset `main-gate`, enforcement active, target `refs/heads/main`:

- pull request required, **required approving reviews: 0** (the human merges by hand; the
  gate is the review), dismiss stale reviews on push, conversation resolution not required,
  `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` off (the API default of on was found
  after the first merge and switched off by the owner on 2026-10-22);
- required status check: **`gate`** (from `gate.yml`), strict (branch up to date);
- deletion blocked, non-fast-forward (force push) blocked;
- no bypass actors: admins included.

## Alternatives

Legacy branch protection (superseded by rulesets); admin bypass for the first PR (would
let the readiness PR skip the gate it introduces); requiring every job by name (D-003).

## Consequences

Applied with `gh api` on 2026-10-22 and recorded in `ai/session/`. Direct pushes to `main`
fail for everyone, including the owner; `.githooks/pre-push` and
`.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` refuse them earlier.

## /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/docs/decisions/D-003-ci-two-workflows-one-check.md
# D-003: Two workflows, one required check, jobs that activate with the code

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

RULES.md rule 6 splits CI into light checks on the mission branch (under three minutes
warm) and a full attested run on the one PR into `main`. The `main` ruleset must name
required checks before any code exists, and a required check that never reports hangs the
final PR.

## Decision

- `mission-branch.yml` (on `mission/**`, also `workflow_call`): docs, links, workflows,
  secrets, rust, deny. Aggregate job **`mission-checks`**.
- `gate.yml` (on PRs to `main`): reuses the light workflow, adds Semgrep, Trivy fs, Checkov
  on the workflows, SBOM (syft), macOS Tauri bundle with `attest-build-provenance` and
  cosign keyless signatures. Aggregate job **`gate`**, the only check the ruleset requires.
- Aggregate jobs run `if: always()` and fail on any `failure`/`cancelled` in `needs`;
  skipped jobs count as not applicable. New jobs are added to `needs`, never to the ruleset.
- Rust, fixtures and Tauri jobs are gated by a `detect` job probing for `Cargo.toml`,
  `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl`, and `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.
- Every action is pinned to a commit digest with a version comment; Renovate keeps them
  current (D-005). Versions verified against GitHub releases on 2026-10-22.
- Workflows call `make` targets so README commands and CI commands are the same thing.

## Alternatives

Listing each job as a required check: brittle, breaks when jobs are renamed or skipped.
Separate workflows per tool: more files, no shared `detect`.

## Consequences

The ruleset (D-007) requires exactly `gate`. The mission must keep the probed paths.

## 5. Mapping (`core::mapping`)

```rust
pub struct MapContext<'a> { pub session: &'a SessionMeta /* id, role, parent, model, mission_id */, pub version: MappingVersion }
pub fn map_record(rec: &RawRecord, ctx: &MapContext) -> Vec<Event>;   // total: ≥ 1 event, never panics
pub fn select_version(droid_version: Option<&str>) -> (MappingVersion, Option<Warning>);
```

Version selection: `0.247.*` → `V1`; any other or `None` → `LATEST` with
`Warning::UnknownDroidVersion { seen, used }` printed once by the CLI and shown once in the UI status bar
(SPEC §5.2). `mapping_version_is_selected_by_droid_version()` reads it from `capture.json`.

`mapping::v1` input shapes (observed in `~/.factory/sessions/…` on 2026-10-22, keys only; M0 confirms
and freezes): line `type` ∈ `session_start`, `message`, `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`,
`compaction_state`. `message` lines: `{id, parentId, seq, timestamp (RFC 3339), message: {role: user|assistant,
content: [ {type: text|thinking|tool_use|tool_result, ...} ], modelId?, apiProvider?, reasoningEffort?}}`.
`tool_use` parts: `{id, name, input}`; `tool_result`: `{tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`. Tool names seen:
`Task`, `Execute`, `Script`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Create`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `LS`, `TodoWrite`, `AskUser`,
`ProposeMission`, `Skill`, `FetchUrl`, `WaitForScript`, `ApplyPatch`.

v1 rules (the frozen table lives in `mapping/v1/kinds.rs` and is reproduced in the M0 decision file):

| Raw shape | EventKind | Lane / role |
|---|---|---|
| `session_start` with no `callingSessionId` | `IntentCreated` (first) | 1, Orchestrator |
| `session_start` with `callingSessionId` | `SubagentSpawned` | 3, child's role |
| user `message`, text, root session, first | `IntentCreated`; later ones `IntentAmended` | 1, Human |
| assistant `tool_use` name `Task` | `TaskAssigned` (+ `FeatureDefined` when the input names a new feature) | 2 |
| assistant `tool_use` name `ProposeMission` | `PlanCreated`; `MilestoneDefined` per milestone in the input | 2 |
| assistant `tool_use` name `AskUser` | `QuestionAsked` | 1 |
| user `tool_result` for an `AskUser` | `IntentAnswered` | 1, Human |
| assistant `tool_use` Execute/Script with `git commit` in the command | `CommitCreated` | 3 |
| assistant `tool_use` Execute/Script with `cargo test`/`make test`/`make check` | `TestsRun`; result `is_error` → `GateCommandFailed` else `GateCommandPassed` when the command is `make check` | 3 / 6 |
| assistant `tool_use` Edit/Create/ApplyPatch | `FileTouched` | 3 |
| `tool_result` with `is_error: true` | `ToolError` (`HookBlocked` when the content names `guard-git.sh`) | 3 |
| assistant message whose `modelId` differs from the previous assistant message of the session | `ModelChanged` | 3 |
| `compaction_state` | `ContextCompacted` | 2 |
| `agent_turn_outcome` in a child session | `TaskDone` (`resultKind`), then `SubagentFinished` at EOF | 3 |
| `todo_state` | `PlanRevised` when todos changed | 2 |
| validator text containing a `## Blocking`/`## Non-blocking` findings block (format fixed in M0 from the capture) | `FindingBlocking` / `FindingNonBlocking` / `ScrutinyPassed`; user-testing `QaScenarioPassed/Failed/Evidence` | 4 / 5 |
| sidecar `tokenUsage` (per session, emitted once at EOF or when it changes) | `UsageReported` with `TokenUsage` | 3 (role's lane) |
| anything else | `Unknown { raw_type: "<type>" or "<type>/<content type>/<tool name>" }` | `Lane::for_role(role)` |

Role resolution (`mapping/v1/roles.rs`), in order: (1) no `callingSessionId` → `Orchestrator`;
(2) the parent's `tool_use` part whose `id == callingToolUseId` has `input.subagent_type` (observed:
`worker`); `worker` → `Worker`, values containing `scrutiny` → `ScrutinyValidator`, `user` + `test` →
`UserTestingValidator` (exact strings fixed in M0); (3) `tags` entry `role:<x>`; (4) else `Unresolved`.
Ids (`mapping/v1/ids.rs`): `mission_id` = root session id; `milestone_id`/`feature_id` from the `Task`
input's `description`/title matched against the `ProposeMission` plan (M0 fixes the exact fields).
Model = assistant `modelId`, else sidecar `model`.

Golden tests (`tests/mapping.rs`): for each `fixtures/streams/*.capture.json`, map the capture with the
header's version and compare to `<...>.events.json` (array of `Event`, paths relative to repo root,
