## 2. Mission setup

**Command** (run by the owner from the repository root on a checkout of `main` that contains this
approved spec; the mission creates `mission/observatory-v1` from it):

```sh
droid exec --mission --auto high \
  --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort high \
  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
  --output-format text \
  -f SPEC.md
```

| Flag | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `--mission --auto high` | required | Missions auto-approve proposals and need `--auto high` (Droid 0.247.0 `droid exec --help`). The hooks in `.factory/hooks.json` are the guard, not the prompt. |
| `--model` | `claude-fable-5.1` | Orchestrator (D-006, corrected 2026-10-22 from the misspelt `claude-fable-5-1`, which fell back to GPT-6 Sol). Factory catalog id, 4× multiplier. |
| `--reasoning-effort` | `high` | Fable's default; planning and integration are where judgment is bought. `xhigh`/`max` on a 4× model is not justified before a measured need. |
| `--worker-model` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Workers (D-006). 0.8× multiplier. Catalog id per docs.factory.com/models; `droid exec --help` on this machine lists `claude-sonnet-5` but not `claude-sonnet-5-5`; owner confirmed available on 2026-10-22. |
| `--worker-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Owner decision 2026-10-22: the model default; Rust compile errors and Leptos (little training data, PRD §12) need the reasoning. The cost/quality split lane 9 measures is between models, not efforts. |
| `--validator-model` | `claude-opus-5-5` | Validators, scrutiny and user testing (D-006). 1.6× multiplier. |
| `--validator-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Above Opus's default `medium`: validation is where correctness is bought (D-006 alternatives). |
| `--output-format` | `text` | The terminal is for the human; the dataset is the session JSONL under `~/.factory/sessions/`, which attach and replay read. |
| `-f SPEC.md` | this file | The mission plans from the approved spec (template, last paragraph). |

The same values are declared in `.factory/settings.json` so that a mission started from the
Factory App uses them: `missionOrchestratorModel`, `missionOrchestratorReasoningEffort`,
`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `.workerReasoningEffort`, `.validationWorkerModel`,
`.validationWorkerReasoningEffort`. The three reasoning-effort keys are added with the spec PR
(§8). A change to any model is a decision file (rule 19).

**Mission branch.** `mission/observatory-v1`, created from `main` at the commit that contains this
approved spec. One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end of the mission, opened
by the orchestrator, merged by the human after `gate` is green. Nothing else reaches `main`
(rule 12). The branch is deleted at the merge (PRD §2).

**Worktree policy.** One worktree per milestone: `git worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m>
mission/observatory-v1` where `<m>` is `s`, `m0` … `m5`. Workers and validators of a milestone
work only inside its worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13); the shared files
(`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) are written by
the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration. Integration is `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`
into `mission/observatory-v1` by the orchestrator, then `make check` locally, then the
`mission-checks` run on the push must be green before the next milestone starts. A worktree is
removed after integration; its branch stays (history).

**Gate command.** `make check` is the only local gate: it is exactly what `mission-branch.yml`
runs (rule 5). A worker hands off only with `make check` green in its worktree; the orchestrator
integrates only with `make check` green on the mission branch.

**Hooks that must be active.** `.factory/hooks.json`: `guard-git.sh` (PreToolUse on `Execute`,
blocks amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push/push-to-main) and `log-tool-call.sh` (PostToolUse,
appends one JSON line per tool call to `build-log/<UTC-day>/<session>.jsonl`). Git hooks via
`make hooks` (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`): `pre-commit` (gitleaks on staged files, file size, debt
markers, decisions index, rustfmt, markdownlint), `commit-msg` (subject ≤ 72 chars, no WIP/fixup),
`pre-push` (no `main`, no non-fast-forward). A worker that finds a hook missing stops and reports;
it never disables or bypasses one (`--no-verify` is a rule 12 violation).

**Usage budget per milestone.** Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed
from the token counts Factory reports for the mission's sessions (the usage page or the stream's
`usage.reported`), pasted into `reports/usage/<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 7). Factory
Standard Credits are recorded next to it when visible. The caps below are the owner's planning
numbers, not measurements; this is the first mission and there is no prior run to calibrate on.
At the M0 boundary the orchestrator proposes re-caps for M1–M5 from the measured S and M0 usage
(owner decision 2026-10-22); until then the table stands.

| Milestone | Cap (USD-eq) | Reason for the size |
|---|---|---|
| S  walking skeleton | 40 | Thin slice, few files, mostly scaffolding and one fixture. |
| M0 capture and mapping | 60 | Mapper plus golden tests; the capture already exists (§3 M0). |
| M1 board, replay, attach | 150 | Largest UI milestone and the Leptos go/no-go; rework budget inside. |
| M2 host | 80 | RPC adapter plus launch screen; the control channel is new ground. |
| M3 intervention | 60 | Lane-7 semantics over M2 controls; small surface. |
| M4 branch, gate, fix loop | 120 | Two adapters (git, GitHub), the demo branch pair, a live PR loop. |
| M5 time, waste, cost | 120 | The metric engine and its oracle test; export; charts. |
| Total | 630 | Hard stop for the mission; the final PR and fixes come out of the unspent remainder. |

At a cap the orchestrator stops dispatching, writes the usage so far to `reports/usage/`, raises
the stall flag and waits for the human (rule 15). Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9).

**What the human will answer mid-mission.** Only at a milestone boundary or when the stall flag is
up (rule 15): the M1 go/no-go (PRD §12), a budget cap reached, a proposed deviation from this spec
with its reason and cost, a keychain item or GitHub permission the mission cannot create itself
(§3 M4, §5.9), the reference spreadsheet for M5 (B-008), and a red `gate` on the final PR.

**What the human will not answer.** Style, naming, crate choice within §4, test structure, how to
split a milestone into features, which worker does what, or anything already decided here or in
`docs/decisions/`. Those go to the backlog with a reason or into a decision file (rules 13, 14).

## SPEC 5.8
### 5.8 Runtime limits

From §5.5: 64 watched sessions, 512 MB per session file before warnings, 1 MiB tail chunk,
100 ms UI batch, 500 ms JSONL poll, 30 s GitHub poll, 15 s metric export, 20 min stall threshold.
The UI holds at most the visible window of events; everything else is a store query (reason: a
mission can emit tens of thousands of lines; the board must stay at 60 fps on a laptop). The host
child process is reaped on window close (M2 test). No network access except GitHub (when a token
is present) and the OTLP gateway (when enabled); both are shown in a status bar.

Validation and build concurrency (measured 2026-10-22; source:
`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`).
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.

### 5.9 Security

- Secrets only from the macOS keychain or the environment (rule 4): `droid-observatory/github-token`
  or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for lane 8; `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` for telemetry (no environment
  fallback in the app, D-010). Never in config, store, logs or the exported telemetry.
- Raw JSONL is rendered read-only after the B-006 scrub pass, never uploaded, never copied into the
  store (PRD §11.2); rendering read-only and the merge as the one outward write are PRD §11.3.
  Fixtures are committed only after gitleaks and a human read (§3).
- The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5): confirmation names PR number and target branch;
  the app uses the repository's allowed merge method; the action is a lane-7 event.
- Telemetry carries no session id, event id, feature id or free text (D-010); the label allow-list
  is enforced in code and by test.

## SPEC 7
## 7. CI

Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).

**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
decision file.

**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.

**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
`main`.

**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan of
the repository (vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH and CRITICAL; `Cargo.lock` is what makes the vuln
scan meaningful), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`)
with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy results and SBOM
attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the human to a
commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and, from S onward, checks the workspace version against the
tag (B-016, wired in S; D-009).

## commit-msg
#!/bin/sh
# Commit message: first line under 72 characters, non-empty, no WIP.
set -eu
msg_file=$1
first=$(head -n1 "$msg_file")
len=$(printf '%s' "$first" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
if [ -z "$first" ]; then echo "commit-msg: empty subject"; exit 1; fi
if [ "$len" -gt 72 ]; then echo "commit-msg: subject is $len chars, limit 72"; exit 1; fi
case "$first" in
  WIP*|wip*|fixup!*|squash!*) echo "commit-msg: no WIP/fixup/squash commits on shared branches (rule 12)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

## pre-commit
#!/bin/sh
# Pre-commit: fast local checks. Enable with `make hooks`.
# Mirrors the mission-branch CI so a red commit is caught before push (ai/RULES.md rule 6).
set -eu
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "pre-commit: secrets"
if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  gitleaks protect --staged --no-banner --redact
else
  echo "  gitleaks missing (brew install gitleaks); CI will catch secrets, local check skipped"
fi

echo "pre-commit: file size"
MAX_FILE_KB=${MAX_FILE_KB:-200} sh scripts/check-file-size.sh

echo "pre-commit: debt markers"
sh scripts/check-todos.sh

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '^docs/decisions/D-'; then
  echo "pre-commit: decisions index"
  sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh | diff -q docs/decisions/README.md - >/dev/null \
    || { echo "  decisions index stale: run 'make decisions-index' and stage it"; exit 1; }
fi

if [ -f Cargo.toml ] && git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '\.rs$'; then
  echo "pre-commit: rustfmt"
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
fi

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '\.md$' && command -v markdownlint-cli2 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "pre-commit: markdown"
  git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.md$' | xargs markdownlint-cli2
fi

# services.yaml: single source of truth for the commands and local services of the

// @input: init <<'SHEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Per-session preflight for the droid-observatory mission. Idempotent, installs nothing,
# prints no secret values. Run from anywhere; it addresses the repository and the worktree
# by absolute path. Exit 1 only when the hooks that enforce ai/RULES.md rule 12 are not active.
set -euo pipefail

REPO=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
WT=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current
MISSION_BRANCH=mission/observatory-v1
UI_PORT=3141

status=0
say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '  ok       %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '  WARN     %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '  FAIL     %s\n' "$*"; status=1; }

say "== droid-observatory init: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"

say "== versions"
version_of() {
  # $1 = label, rest = command. A missing tool is reported, not fatal: make doctor repeats it.
  label=$1; shift
  if out=$("$@" 2>&1 | head -1); then
    printf '  %-22s %s\n' "$label" "$out"
  else
    printf '  %-22s missing (%s)\n' "$label" "$*"
  fi
}
version_of "droid"            droid --version
version_of "rustc"            rustc --version
version_of "cargo"            cargo --version
version_of "trunk"            trunk --version
version_of "cargo tauri"      cargo tauri --version
version_of "cargo llvm-cov"   cargo llvm-cov --version
version_of "cargo machete"    cargo machete --version
version_of "cargo deny"       cargo deny --version
version_of "agent-browser"    agent-browser --version
version_of "gh"               gh --version
version_of "sqlite3"          sqlite3 --version
version_of "gitleaks"         gitleaks version

say "== machine"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "cores"            "$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"
printf '  %-22s %s GiB\n' "memory"       "$(( $(sysctl -n hw.memsize) / 1024 / 1024 / 1024 ))"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "load (1/5/15 min)" "$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg)"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "CARGO_TARGET_DIR"  "${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-unset (expected /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target)}"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS"  "${CARGO_BUILD_JOBS:-unset (services.yaml env sets 6)}"

say "== repository: $REPO"
if [ ! -d "$REPO/.git" ]; then
  fail "not a git repository: $REPO"
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$REPO" doctor
make -C "$REPO" hooks

repo_branch=$(git -C "$REPO" branch --show-current)
if [ "$repo_branch" = "$MISSION_BRANCH" ]; then
  ok "branch $repo_branch"
elif case "$repo_branch" in wt/*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; then
  warn "repository is on $repo_branch (a milestone worktree branch); expected $MISSION_BRANCH. Not fatal, but integration runs on the mission branch."
else
  warn "repository is on '$repo_branch'; expected $MISSION_BRANCH"
fi
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "HEAD" "$(git -C "$REPO" log -1 --format='%h %s')"

say "== hooks (rule 12 / rule 17)"
hooks_path=$(git -C "$REPO" config core.hooksPath || true)
if [ "$hooks_path" = ".githooks" ]; then ok "core.hooksPath=.githooks"; else fail "core.hooksPath is '$hooks_path', expected .githooks (make hooks)"; fi
for h in pre-commit commit-msg pre-push; do
  if [ -x "$REPO/.githooks/$h" ]; then ok ".githooks/$h executable"; else fail ".githooks/$h missing or not executable"; fi
done
if [ -f "$REPO/.factory/hooks.json" ]; then ok ".factory/hooks.json present"; else fail ".factory/hooks.json missing"; fi
for h in guard-git.sh log-tool-call.sh; do
  if [ -x "$REPO/.factory/hooks/$h" ]; then ok ".factory/hooks/$h executable"; else fail ".factory/hooks/$h missing or not executable"; fi
done
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "jq present (hooks need it)"; else fail "jq missing: .factory hooks cannot run (brew install jq)"; fi
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  say "hooks are not active: stop and report (docs/runbooks/hooks-disabled.md). Never disable or bypass a hook."
  exit 1
fi

say "== secrets (presence only, values never read)"
for item in github-token otlp-headers; do
  if security find-generic-password -s "droid-observatory/$item" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "keychain droid-observatory/$item present"
  else
    warn "keychain droid-observatory/$item absent"
  fi
done
if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then ok "GITHUB_TOKEN set in environment (fallback for the token only)"; else ok "GITHUB_TOKEN not set (keychain is the primary source)"; fi

say "== port $UI_PORT"
listeners=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:"$UI_PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN -Fpc 2>/dev/null | paste -sd' ' - || true)
if [ -z "$listeners" ]; then
  ok "free"
else
  # lsof -F output: p<pid> c<command> pairs
  owner_cmd=$(printf '%s' "$listeners" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^c//p' | head -1)
  owner_pid=$(printf '%s' "$listeners" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^p//p' | head -1)
  if [ "$owner_cmd" = "trunk" ]; then
    ok "owned by trunk (pid $owner_pid): reuse it; do not start a second trunk on $UI_PORT"
  else
    warn "owned by '$owner_cmd' (pid $owner_pid), not a trunk process. Do not kill it blindly; use a scratch port 3142-3149 or ask."
  fi
fi

say "== worktree symlink: $WT"
if [ ! -e "$WT" ]; then
  if [ -L "$WT" ]; then
    warn "symlink exists but its target is missing: $(readlink "$WT")"
  fi
  say "  The active-milestone worktree is not in place. The integration feature (or the orchestrator) creates it:"
  say "    git -C $REPO worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m> $MISSION_BRANCH"
  say "    ln -sfn /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m> $WT"
  say "  init.sh does not create worktrees. Exiting 0."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Per-session preflight for the droid-observatory mission. Idempotent, installs nothing,
# prints no secret values. Run from anywhere; it addresses the repository and the worktree
# by absolute path. Exit 1 only when the hooks that enforce ai/RULES.md rule 12 are not active.
set -euo pipefail

REPO=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
WT=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current
MISSION_BRANCH=mission/observatory-v1
UI_PORT=3141

status=0
say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '  ok       %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '  WARN     %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '  FAIL     %s\n' "$*"; status=1; }

say "== droid-observatory init: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"

say "== versions"
version_of() {
  # $1 = label, rest = command. A missing tool is reported, not fatal: make doctor repeats it.
  label=$1; shift
  if out=$("$@" 2>&1 | head -1); then
    printf '  %-22s %s\n' "$label" "$out"
  else
    printf '  %-22s missing (%s)\n' "$label" "$*"
  fi
}
version_of "droid"            droid --version
version_of "rustc"            rustc --version
version_of "cargo"            cargo --version
version_of "trunk"            trunk --version
version_of "cargo tauri"      cargo tauri --version
version_of "cargo llvm-cov"   cargo llvm-cov --version
version_of "cargo machete"    cargo machete --version
version_of "cargo deny"       cargo deny --version
version_of "agent-browser"    agent-browser --version
version_of "gh"               gh --version
version_of "sqlite3"          sqlite3 --version
version_of "gitleaks"         gitleaks version

say "== machine"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "cores"            "$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"
printf '  %-22s %s GiB\n' "memory"       "$(( $(sysctl -n hw.memsize) / 1024 / 1024 / 1024 ))"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "load (1/5/15 min)" "$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg)"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "CARGO_TARGET_DIR"  "${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-unset (expected /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target)}"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS"  "${CARGO_BUILD_JOBS:-unset (services.yaml env sets 6)}"

say "== repository: $REPO"
if [ ! -d "$REPO/.git" ]; then
  fail "not a git repository: $REPO"
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$REPO" doctor
make -C "$REPO" hooks

repo_branch=$(git -C "$REPO" branch --show-current)
if [ "$repo_branch" = "$MISSION_BRANCH" ]; then
  ok "branch $repo_branch"
elif case "$repo_branch" in wt/*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; then
  warn "repository is on $repo_branch (a milestone worktree branch); expected $MISSION_BRANCH. Not fatal, but integration runs on the mission branch."
else
  warn "repository is on '$repo_branch'; expected $MISSION_BRANCH"
fi
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "HEAD" "$(git -C "$REPO" log -1 --format='%h %s')"

say "== hooks (rule 12 / rule 17)"
hooks_path=$(git -C "$REPO" config core.hooksPath || true)
if [ "$hooks_path" = ".githooks" ]; then ok "core.hooksPath=.githooks"; else fail "core.hooksPath is '$hooks_path', expected .githooks (make hooks)"; fi
for h in pre-commit commit-msg pre-push; do
  if [ -x "$REPO/.githooks/$h" ]; then ok ".githooks/$h executable"; else fail ".githooks/$h missing or not executable"; fi
done
if [ -f "$REPO/.factory/hooks.json" ]; then ok ".factory/hooks.json present"; else fail ".factory/hooks.json missing"; fi
for h in guard-git.sh log-tool-call.sh; do
  if [ -x "$REPO/.factory/hooks/$h" ]; then ok ".factory/hooks/$h executable"; else fail ".factory/hooks/$h missing or not executable"; fi
done
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "jq present (hooks need it)"; else fail "jq missing: .factory hooks cannot run (brew install jq)"; fi
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  say "hooks are not active: stop and report (docs/runbooks/hooks-disabled.md). Never disable or bypass a hook."
  exit 1
fi

say "== secrets (presence only, values never read)"
for item in github-token otlp-headers; do
  if security find-generic-password -s "droid-observatory/$item" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "keychain droid-observatory/$item present"
  else
    warn "keychain droid-observatory/$item absent"
  fi
done
if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then ok "GITHUB_TOKEN set in environment (fallback for the token only)"; else ok "GITHUB_TOKEN not set (keychain is the primary source)"; fi

say "== port $UI_PORT"
listeners=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:"$UI_PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN -Fpc 2>/dev/null | paste -sd' ' - || true)
if [ -z "$listeners" ]; then
  ok "free"
else
  # lsof -F output: p<pid> c<command> pairs
  owner_cmd=$(printf '%s' "$listeners" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^c//p' | head -1)
  owner_pid=$(printf '%s' "$listeners" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^p//p' | head -1)
  if [ "$owner_cmd" = "trunk" ]; then
    ok "owned by trunk (pid $owner_pid): reuse it; do not start a second trunk on $UI_PORT"
  else
    warn "owned by '$owner_cmd' (pid $owner_pid), not a trunk process. Do not kill it blindly; use a scratch port 3142-3149 or ask."
  fi
fi

say "== worktree symlink: $WT"
if [ ! -e "$WT" ]; then
  if [ -L "$WT" ]; then
    warn "symlink exists but its target is missing: $(readlink "$WT")"
  fi
  say "  The active-milestone worktree is not in place. The integration feature (or the orchestrator) creates it:"
  say "    git -C $REPO worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m> $MISSION_BRANCH"
  say "    ln -sfn /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m> $WT"
  say "  init.sh does not create worktrees. Exiting 0."
  exit 0
fi
wt_real=$(cd "$WT" && pwd -P)
wt_top=$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$wt_top" ]; then
  fail "$WT is not inside a git work tree"
  exit 1
fi
wt_common=$(cd "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --git-common-dir)" && pwd -P)
repo_git=$(cd "$REPO/.git" && pwd -P)
if [ "$wt_common" = "$repo_git" ]; then
  ok "worktree of $REPO (common dir $wt_common)"
else
  warn "git common dir is $wt_common, not $repo_git: this is not a worktree of the mission repository"
fi
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "target"  "$wt_real"
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "toplevel" "$wt_top"
wt_branch=$(git -C "$WT" branch --show-current)
case "$wt_branch" in
  wt/*) ok "branch $wt_branch" ;;
  *)    warn "worktree branch is '$wt_branch'; expected wt/<m>" ;;
esac
printf '  %-22s %s\n' "HEAD" "$(git -C "$WT" log -1 --format='%h %s')"
# core.hooksPath is a relative path resolved from the worktree top, so the shared config covers it;
# this only confirms the hook files travelled with the checkout.
if [ -x "$WT/.githooks/pre-commit" ] && [ -f "$WT/.factory/hooks.json" ]; then
  ok "hooks present in the worktree checkout"
else
  fail "hooks missing in the worktree checkout"
fi
if [ -n "$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
  warn "worktree has uncommitted tracked changes:"
  git -C "$WT" status --short --untracked-files=no | sed 's/^/           /'
else
  ok "worktree clean (tracked files)"
fi

say "== done (exit $status)"
exit "$status"

// @input: env <<'MDEOF'
# Environment

**What belongs here:** facts about the owner's machine, the toolchain, the cargo and keychain quirks,
the GitHub token, the OTLP header, the Droid install and session directory. Everything is pasted from a
tool or from `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-*.md`; nothing is estimated.

**What does not belong here:** ports, start/stop/healthcheck commands of the mission's own services
(`services.yaml` is the single source), the session-file schema (`droid-sessions.md`), test procedures
(`user-testing.md`), CI and GitHub workflow facts (`github-and-ci.md`).

## Machine

Pasted 2026-10-22 (`sysctl`, `sw_vers`, `uname -r`):

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Cores (`hw.ncpu`) | 10 |
| Memory (`hw.memsize`) | 68719476736 bytes = 64 GiB |
| macOS | 26.0, build 25A354; kernel darwin 25.0.0 |
| Load at the readiness run | `load averages: 3,05 6,26 9,34` (baseline 3-10) |
| Load at drafting | `{ 2,36 4,44 4,44 }` |
| `memory_pressure` at the readiness run | about 60 % free with 7 rustc + 2 Chrome sessions + the Tauri app |

Headroom rule from the validation readiness report: use at most 7 cores and 44.8 GB. Memory is not the
constraint on this machine; CPU and the shared cargo target lock are. The locale prints decimal commas
(`ps` shows `43,0`); convert before summing. `top` is rejected as interactive: sample with
`ps -axo pid,ppid,rss,%cpu,command` and `sysctl -n vm.loadavg`.

## Owner services and off-limits ports

Off-limits (planning notes): 5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444-18451 and anything already listening. The
owner's Docker, Ollama and SurrealDB services are not ours to stop. Listeners pasted at drafting
(`lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN`, browser processes filtered out):

```text

ControlCe 599 *:7000

```

Ours: 3141 for the UI dev server (one `trunk serve` at a time), 3142-3149 scratch. Both were free at
planning; `init.sh` reports the state of 3141 at every session start.

## Toolchain versions (pasted 2026-10-22)

| Tool | Output of `--version` |
|---|---|
| Droid | `0.247.0` |
| rustc | `rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13)` (pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`: 1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target) |

| sqlite3 | `3.51.0 2025-06-12` |
| gitleaks | `8.30.1` |
| markdownlint-cli2 | `v0.24.0 (markdownlint v0.42.0)` |
| lychee | `lychee 0.24.2` |

`make doctor` reports every required tool ok. Nothing is installed per session (`init.sh` only re-runs
`make doctor` and `make hooks`). Install times when the tools were added (dependency readiness report):
trunk 579 s (incl. lock wait), tauri-cli 305 s, cargo-llvm-cov 98 s, cargo-machete 58 s, cargo-deny 174 s.
`rust-toolchain.toml` is not changed without a decision file.

## Cargo quirks

- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target` is set in the shell environment, not in
  `~/.cargo/config.toml`. Every cargo-driven build (cargo test, trunk, cargo tauri dev) shares one build

  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs` (`replay_s.rs`, `mapping.rs`, `store.rs`, `attach_latency.rs`, `view.rs`,

  with `assert_cmd`). Fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`.
- Test functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`,
  `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file()`.
- UI logic is unit-tested in `core::view`; there is no wasm test runner. The UI crate gets `cargo check`
  only.
- Coverage scope is `observatory-core` only: `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80`,
  reported in S, enforced from M0. It runs alone (see `services.yaml`).
- Golden files (`<fixture>.events.json`) are regenerated only with
  `OBSERVATORY_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` and a reviewer read.
- Flaky timing tests (attach latency) are reported with their `p50/p95/max`, never retried silently.

## Red before green (rule 1)

The failing test is committed before the code that makes it pass; the scrutiny validator checks that the
red run exists in the worker log. Pattern per feature:

1. Write the test, run it, paste the failing output into the handoff.
2. Commit the red test. Subject example: `test(core): red — rework_window_closes_on_resolution`.
3. Write the code, run the test green, run `make check`.
4. Commit the code. Subject example: `feat(core): close rework windows on resolution — green`.

Commit rules enforced by `.githooks/commit-msg`: subject non-empty and at most 72 characters, no
`WIP`/`fixup!`/`squash!`. Every agent commit carries the trailer
`Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. Pass
multi-line messages through a quoted heredoc (`git commit -F - <<'MSG' ... MSG`). Forward only: never
amend, reset, rebase, stash or force-push; a fix is a new commit (`.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and
`.githooks/pre-push` refuse the rest; `--no-verify` is a rule 12 violation).

- No magic numbers: every threshold and interval lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason
  comment, and `Config::default()` must equal that file (`example_config_equals_defaults()`). A new key is
  added to the example file with its reason in the same commit.
- Debt markers are `TODO(B-NNN)` (or `TODO(#123)`); anything else fails `make check-todos`. Deferred work is
  a `BACKLOG.md` row with a reason (planning note 9: no GitHub issues).
- A dependency is added only with `make deny` green and a version verified on the day (rule 3). `cargo deny`
  covers advisories, licences, bans and sources (`deny.toml`); a new licence is a decision file. Only
  crates.io sources.

  | Crate | Version |
  |---|---|
  | `serde` (derive) | 1.0.229 |
  | `serde_json` | 1.0.154 |

  | `tracing` | 0.1.44 |
  | `tracing-subscriber` (`env-filter`) | 0.3.23 |
  | `tokio` (`rt-multi-thread, process, macros`, app only) | 1.54.1 |
  | `tauri` | 2.12.5 |
  | `leptos` (`csr`) | 0.8.22 |
  | `wasm-bindgen` | 0.2.129 |
  | `opentelemetry` / `opentelemetry_sdk` / `opentelemetry-otlp` | 0.33.1 |
  | `tracing-opentelemetry` | 0.34.0 |
  | `toml`, `time` 0.3.x, `thiserror` 2.x, `anyhow`, `clap` 4.x, `regex`, `ureq` 3.x, `csv` 1.x, `tauri-build` 2.x, `tauri-plugin-dialog` 2.x, `wasm-bindgen-futures`, `js-sys`, `web-sys`, `serde-wasm-bindgen`, dev `tempfile`, `assert_cmd`, `predicates` | verify |

  `keyring` 4.2.0 is rejected: RUSTSEC-2026-0370/0371/0372 via zbus/zvariant on its Linux path.

## Architectural invariants (architecture §1, blocking findings when violated)

- I1: `observatory-core` is synchronous. No `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API; tokio lives only in
  `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`.
- I2: the UI holds no logic. Card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details and library entries are
  functions in `core::view`; the Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends.
- I3: raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store (pointer `path, byte_offset, byte_len`;
  re-read on demand). `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
- I4: every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`.
- I5: unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, counted and shown (`unknown events: N`),
  never dropped. `mapping::map_record` is total.
- I6: thresholds come only from `Config`.
- I7: secrets come only from the keychain (or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the token); never in config, store, logs,
  telemetry or fixtures.
- I8: the one outward write is the merge, human-confirmed; `policy-merged` is observed, not performed.
- I9: core modules compiled to wasm (`model`, `mapping`, `view`, `metrics`, `config`) have no platform
  dependency; platform modules sit behind Cargo features (`store`, `watch`, `rpc`, `github`, `secrets`);
  the UI depends on core with `default-features = false`.

## Fixtures

- Committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean on them and a reviewer read them. Files over
  200 KB are allowed only under `fixtures/streams/` and `build-log/`.

```sh

agent-browser open http://localhost:3141          # 1.25 s
agent-browser snapshot                            # accessibility tree with refs: heading ... [ref=e1], button ... [ref=e2]
agent-browser snapshot -i                         # interactive elements only
agent-browser click @e2                           # click by ref
agent-browser get title
agent-browser get text body

agent-browser console                             # expect empty
```

# Droid session files

**What belongs here:** everything known about the files Droid 0.247.0 writes under `~/.factory/sessions/`,
which `mapping::v1` reads (planning note 1, dependency readiness report, architecture §4-§5), plus the
fixture layout and header. Facts are from the readiness report or from a keys-only inspection of this
mission's own session directory at drafting time (2026-10-22, 24 `.jsonl`); values were not read except
tag names, model ids, tool names and `subagent_type`. Items marked "M0 to confirm" are frozen by the M0
mapping worker in the decision file.

**What does not belong here:** the mapping table itself (architecture §5 and `mapping/v1/kinds.rs`), Rust
conventions, environment facts other than the directory path.

## Directory and file set

- Directory: `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/` where the slug is the working directory with `/` replaced by
  `-`: `~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/`.
- Flat: no subdirectories. Child sessions are sibling files.
- Per session `<session-id>` (UUID): `<id>.jsonl` (the transcript), `<id>.settings.json` (the sidecar),
  `<id>.settings.json.bak`. Counts at drafting: 72 entries = 24 of each. The readiness report saw 12, then
  14 `.jsonl`.
- There is no Droid version anywhere in these files. The mapping version is selected from `droid_version` in
  the fixture header (`0.247.*` maps to `V1`; anything else gives `LATEST` with
  `Warning::UnknownDroidVersion`); a live attach records `droid --version` into the `captures` row.
- The directory is read-only for the mission. Fixtures are byte-identical copies.

## JSONL line types

`type` values and counts over the 24 files at drafting:

```text
3890 message
  54 agent_turn_outcome
  37 todo_state
  24 session_start
   5 compaction_state
```

### `session_start` (first line of each file)

Keys observed (two shapes):

```text
["callingSessionId","callingToolUseId","cwd","hostId","id","isSessionTitleManuallySet","organizationId","owner","title","type","version"]   child
["cwd","hostId","id","isSessionTitleManuallySet","organizationId","owner","sessionTitleAutoStage","title","type","version"]                root
```

- `version` is the numeric schema version: `2` on all 24 files. It is not the Droid version.
- `callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId` are the parent linkage: a file whose `callingSessionId` equals a
  known session id is a child; the root has none. At drafting: 2 roots, 22 children. The root `id` is the
  mission id used by the mapper (`mission_id` = root session id).
- `callingToolUseId` matches the `id` of a `tool_use` part (tool `Task`) in the parent's transcript; the two id
  styles seen are `toolu_bdrk_...` and `call_...`.

### `message`

Top-level keys: `id, message, parentId, seq, timestamp, type` (3601 lines); 265 lines add
`compactionSummaryId`; the 24 first messages have no `parentId`. `timestamp` is RFC 3339.

`message` object keys:

- user: `content, role, visibility` and often `userMessageSource`.
- assistant: `apiProvider, content, modelId, reasoningEffort, role` (211 lines carry these three model keys).
  `modelId` values at drafting: `claude-fable-5.1` (369), `gpt-6.1-sol` (23), `gpt-6-sol` (15).
  A change of `modelId` between consecutive assistant messages of one session is `ModelChanged`.

`content[]` part `type` counts: `tool_use` 1661, `tool_result` 1659, `text` 410, `thinking` 263.
`tool_use` parts: `{id, name, input}`; `tool_result`: `{tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`.
Tool names seen (architecture §5): `Task`, `Execute`, `Script`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Create`, `Grep`, `Glob`,
`LS`, `TodoWrite`, `AskUser`, `ProposeMission`, `Skill`, `FetchUrl`, `WaitForScript`, `ApplyPatch`.

`Task` input keys observed: `await, complexity, description, prompt, subagent_type` (16), without
`complexity` (4), without `await` (2). `subagent_type` values: `worker` (20), `explorer` (2). No validator
spawn exists yet in this directory; the exact `subagent_type` strings for the scrutiny and user-testing
validators are **M0 to confirm** from the S capture.

### `agent_turn_outcome`

Keys `reason, resultKind, turnId, type`. `resultKind` values: `text` (42), `null` (12). In a child session it
maps to `TaskDone`, then `SubagentFinished` at EOF.

### `todo_state`

Keys `id, messageIndex, timestamp, todos, type`. Maps to `PlanRevised` when the todos changed.

### `compaction_state`

Keys `anchorMessage, id, loadedDeferredToolNames, removedCount, retainedImages, retainedSkills, summaryKind,
summaryText, summaryTokens, systemInfo, systemInfoText, timestamp, type`. Maps to `ContextCompacted`.
`summaryText` is free text and is never logged or exported.

## Sidecar `<id>.settings.json`

Keys present on all 24 files: `tokenUsage, inclusiveTokenUsage, lastCallTokenUsage,
childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId, assistantActiveTimeMs, model, reasoningEffort, interactionMode,
autonomyLevel, autonomyMode, toolExecutionMode, toolExecutionModeModelId, providerLock, providerLockTimestamp,
apiProviderLock, compactionThresholdCheckEnabled, allowSubagentsInScripts`. On most: `tags` (23),
`systemPrompt` (22), `disabledToolIds` (22); on a few: `enabledToolIds` (3), `artifacts` (3).

- `tokenUsage` keys: `inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens, thinkingTokens,
  factoryCredits`. The same shape for `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage` and each value of
  `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId` (keyed by child session id). This is where usage lives: there are
  no `usage.reported` lines in the JSONL. The mapper emits `UsageReported` from it once at EOF or when it
  changes.
- `model` values at drafting: `claude-fable-5.1` (19), `gpt-6.1-sol` (5). Model = assistant `modelId`, else
  sidecar `model`.
- `tags` is an array of objects `{ "name": <string>, "metadata": <object|null> }`, not an array of strings.
  Shapes observed:

  ```text
  { "name": "mission-session", "metadata": { "role": "orchestrator", "missionId": "<mission dir id>" } }   1 (the orchestrator)
  { "name": "subagent",        "metadata": { "callingSessionId": "<id>", "callingToolUseId": "<id>" } }  20
  { "name": "read-only",       "metadata": null }                                                       2
  ```

  `missionId` equals the Factory mission directory id (`~/.factory/missions/<missionId>`). Architecture §5
  step (3) of role resolution describes a `role:<x>` tag entry; the real shape is `metadata.role` on the
  `mission-session` tag, present only for the orchestrator so far. **M0 to confirm** whether workers and
  validators get a `role` in their tags and whether `droid exec --tag` values appear here or elsewhere.
- `systemPrompt` is never logged or stored. Unknown keys are ignored by `ingest::sidecar`.

## Ids and roles: what is known and what M0 confirms

| Need | Source today | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `mission_id` | root session id (`session_start.id` with no `callingSessionId`); cross-check `tags[].metadata.missionId` | known |
| parent / child | `session_start.callingSessionId`, `callingToolUseId`; `tags[name=subagent].metadata` repeats both | known |
| role | (1) no `callingSessionId` = orchestrator; (2) parent's `Task` part with `id == callingToolUseId`: `input.subagent_type` (`worker` seen); (3) `tags[].metadata.role`; (4) `Unresolved` | validator strings M0 to confirm |
| `milestone_id`, `feature_id` | `Task` input `description`/`prompt` matched against the `ProposeMission` plan | exact fields M0 to confirm |
| `--tag` values | not observed in this directory | M0 to confirm (where they land, if at all) |
| Droid version | absent from all files | fixture header / `droid --version` at attach |
| validator findings format (`## Blocking` / `## Non-blocking` blocks) | validator text in child sessions | M0 to confirm from the S capture |

## Fixture layout (architecture §4)

```text
fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl                    orchestrator session (byte-identical copy)
fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.capture.json             fixture header
fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.events.json              golden lane events
fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.settings.json            the root's sidecar
fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.children/<id>.jsonl      child sessions, byte-identical copies
fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.children/<id>.settings.json
```

The header is a sidecar, not a first line, so every `byte_offset` in the golden file equals the offset in
the live file:

```json
{ "schema": 1, "droid_version": "0.247.0", "captured_at": "2026-10-22T18:00:00Z",
  "source_dir": "~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory",
  "mission_name": "observatory-v1", "mapping_version": "v1",
  "sessions": [ { "id": "<uuid>", "role": "orchestrator", "file": "2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl" },
                { "id": "<uuid>", "role": "worker", "file": "2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.children/<uuid>.jsonl" } ],
  "captured_with": "droid --version", "gitleaks": "clean 2026-10-22", "reviewed_by": "dct" }
```

`sessions[].role` is the capture's known outcome used by the role-resolution test, not an input to the mapper.
Fixture names: `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl`; S snapshot `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`, M0 capture
`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` frozen from this mission's own sessions at S integration. Commit only
after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean and a reviewer read them; files over 200 KB are allowed here.

## Reading rules for the tailer (architecture §4.2)

Open read-only; read from the stored offset in `tail_chunk_kb` (1024) chunks; split on `\n`; keep an
incomplete trailing fragment until the newline arrives (the writer may be mid-line); `byte_offset` is the first
byte of the line, `byte_len` excludes the newline; a non-JSON line is still a record
(`Unknown { raw_type: "<unparseable>" }`); files over `max_session_file_mb` (512) warn once. Poll every
`jsonl_poll_ms` (500) beside FSEvents; attach files modified in the last `startup_scan_hours` (24); tail at
most `max_watched_sessions` (64).

# User testing

**What belongs here:** the surfaces a validator can drive, the exact commands that worked on this machine
(validation readiness report, 2026-10-22), the oracle commands, the evidence to collect, the cost class of
each surface and how validators isolate from each other. Sections marked "to be filled by validators"
collect runtime findings as milestones land.

**What does not belong here:** start/stop/healthcheck commands and ports (`services.yaml`), machine facts
(`environment.md`), Rust test conventions (`rust-conventions.md`).

## Surfaces at a glance

| Surface | What it proves | Driver | Cost class |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI (`observatory-cli replay`, `inspect`, `metrics --csv`) and `cargo test` | mapping, counts, pointers, metrics; the oracle for everything else | shell | low (warm `cargo test` 2.6 s in the scratch crate) |
| Browser host: `trunk serve` on 3141 | the board and every view-model in a real browser (primary interactive surface, SPEC §6) | `agent-browser` | medium: trunk 35 MB idle, each browser session 1.34-1.54 GB RSS, max 3 sessions |
| Tauri window: `make app-dev` | the native shell starts, loads the same UI, wires commands (smoke check, planning note 4) | `ps`, log, `lsof`, `osascript`, `screencapture` | high during the build (37.66 s to the app process, native rustc burst), low idle (130 MB RSS) |
| Live attach / host | a real `droid exec --mission` appears on the board within 1 s (M1), hosted mission controls (M2) | terminal + board | medium (a Droid session plus the board) |
| `cargo llvm-cov` | coverage floor | shell | high: load 3.3 to 14.6 on 10 cores; runs alone |
| GitHub via `gh api` | PR, runs, statuses, rulesets for the gate lane (M4) | `gh` | low |

Serialize anything that compiles: cargo builds share the `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `cargo llvm-cov` and the
first `cargo tauri dev` build run with nothing else compiling. Validators run user tests only after builds
finish.

## Browser host (primary)

Start `trunk-ui` from `services.yaml` and wait for `curl -sf http://localhost:3141/` (55.94 s cold, then
1.46-2.08 s per incremental rebuild). Then, exactly as they worked on 2026-10-22:

```sh
until curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:3141/; do sleep 1; done
agent-browser open http://localhost:3141          # 1.25 s
agent-browser snapshot                            # accessibility tree with refs: heading ... [ref=e1], button ... [ref=e2]
agent-browser snapshot -i                         # interactive elements only
agent-browser click @e2                           # click by ref
agent-browser get title
agent-browser get text body
agent-browser screenshot /tmp/observatory-<milestone>-<scenario>.png
agent-browser console                             # expect empty
agent-browser errors                              # expect empty
agent-browser --session <name> open http://localhost:3141   # isolated second validator (own Chrome, own page state)
agent-browser session list
agent-browser close --all                         # at the end; daemons otherwise linger 1 h
```

Rules:

- One `--session <name>` per validator (`default` is a session too); at most 3 sessions per `trunk serve`;
  never more than 5. Sessions are isolated (verified: `clicks: 1` in `default` while `val2` showed `clicks: 0`).
- Read the page through `snapshot`, not the raw HTML: the dev page carries trunk's live-reload script
  (websocket `/.well-known/trunk/ws`) at the top of `<body>`; the app is inside `<main>`.
- Evidence per scenario: the snapshot lines you asserted on (with refs), the screenshot path and byte size
  (`Screenshot saved to ... (12217 bytes)` style), `console` and `errors` output, and the CLI oracle output
  for the same fixture.
- `agent-browser` cannot attach to the Tauri window (no CDP endpoint; `connect 9229` fails with
  `All CDP discovery methods failed`). A failed `connect` leaves a daemon entry; close it.

### Opening a fixture in the browser host

The UI's `BrowserBackend` (architecture §7) reads the fixture through an `<input type=file>` file picker,
runs `mapping::map_record` and `core::view` in wasm, with no store. The exact agent-browser steps (which ref
the input has, which command sets a file on it, whether a `.capture.json` or the root `.jsonl` is picked,
how the children directory is supplied) are not known until the UI exists.

**To be filled by the M1 ui-worker:** the exact commands, the expected `MissionSummary` text on screen
(`event_count`, `unknown_count`, `mapping_version`) and the fixture used
(`fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl`).

## Tauri window (smoke check)

Owner decision (planning note 4): the Tauri window is validated as a smoke check; the functional evidence is
the browser host. Procedure, with the commands that worked:

1. Make sure no other trunk owns 3141 (`lsof -nP -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:LISTEN`, exit 1 = free), then start
   `tauri-dev` from `services.yaml` (log `/tmp/observatory-tauri.log`).
2. Wait for the line `Running /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target/debug/observatory-app` in the log
   (37.66 s after launch with warm wasm; 31.18 s of it is the native build) and check that no panic follows.
3. Process alive:

   ```sh
   ps -axo pid,command | awk '$2 ~ /shared_rust_target\/debug\/observatory-app$/ {print $1}'
   ps -p <pid> -o pid,rss,%cpu,command          # 130 MB RSS, 0.0 %CPU idle in the readiness run
   ```

4. The webview fetched the page: `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` shows `com.apple.WebKit` (or `com.apple ...`)
   `ESTABLISHED` connections to `[::1]:3141` (three in the readiness run).
5. System Events lists the app as a foreground process:

   ```sh
   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process whose background only is false'
   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get {name, unix id, frontmost, visible} of process "observatory-app"'
   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "observatory-app" to count windows'   # 1 when the display is unlocked
   ```

6. Screenshot only when the display is unlocked: check
   `ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | grep -A1 CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` first; locked gives a uniformly black frame
   (`YAVG=16`) and `count windows` 0. Then `screencapture -x /tmp/observatory-tauri-<milestone>.png` and verify
   with `ffmpeg -hide_banner -i <png> -vf signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=- -f null - 2>/dev/null | grep YAVG`.
   If the display is locked, record process/log/System-Events evidence and say so; the owner's screenshot
   (below) is the human-captured frame.
7. Shutdown: kill cargo-tauri, `trunk serve` and the app binary by PID (killing cargo-tauri alone orphans the
   other two, trunk keeps 3141 bound). `services.yaml` `tauri-dev.stop` does this. Confirm with
   `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:LISTEN` (exit 1) and the System Events list.

Whether a window-level screenshot works on an unlocked screen is unverified (the readiness run had the
screen locked). **To be filled by validators:** the first unlocked `count windows` and `screencapture` result,
with the window title (`app.windows[].title`, `droid-observatory`).

## CLI oracle

All from the worktree (`services.yaml` `replay`, `inspect`, `metrics-csv`):

```sh
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl        # prints lane events, ends with `unknown events: N`; exit 0
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay /nonexistent.jsonl; echo $?           # non-zero (cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file)
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- inspect <event-id>                             # the exact raw bytes of the line by pointer; `--scrub` applies the B-006 pass
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl --csv # M5; compared to reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv within 1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD
make replay-fixtures                                                              # every fixture, exit 1 on the first failure
```

The last line of `replay` and the tray count on the board must agree; `inspect` output must equal the
byte slice `dd if=<file> bs=1 skip=<byte_offset> count=<byte_len>` of the fixture. M0 gate: `unknown events: 0`
on the M0 capture; S allows N > 0.

## Store

`[store].path` defaults to `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`; a validator overrides it through a temp
config (`OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<path>`, see Isolation). Inspect read-only:

```sh
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite '.tables'
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite 'select count(*) from events;'
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite 'select * from mapping_versions; select * from captures;'
```

Invariant to check: no payload column; rows carry `path, byte_offset, byte_len` only (I3). Table and column
names are the M0 store-worker's; **to be filled by the M0 validators** once `migrations/0001_init.sql`
exists.

## GitHub (gate lane, M4)

Read with the owner's `gh` login (`dctellya`, admin) or the read-only PAT; never the check-runs API:

```sh
gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>             # runs for a commit
gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/commits/<sha>/status                     # combined commit status
gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/rulesets                                 # main-gate id 25636994, demo-gate (M4)
gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/pulls/<n>                                # PR state, labels, mergeable
gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus,labels,statusCheckRollup
gh run list --branch <branch> --limit 10
gh run view <run-id>                                                             # created / updated timestamps, conclusion
```

Paste run ids, PR numbers, SHAs and timestamps into the evidence; the M4 scenario needs every one of them
(`demo/red-1` PR with `demo:red`, failing run id, label removal, green run id, merge, badge).

## Live attach and host

- Attach (M1): with the board open, start a `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal on a scratch directory
  inside the worktree (`target/scratch/<name>`); the new session must appear on the board and each event
  within 1 s. Latency evidence: the `attach_latency.rs` harness output (`p50/p95/max`, pasted) plus validator
  wall-clock timestamps.
- Host (M2): a short hosted mission on a scratch directory inside the worktree; pause, message and answer
  reach the orchestrator; hosted and attached views agree on the event count; the child process is reaped on
  window close.
- `~/.factory/sessions/` is read-only; never delete or edit the files a live run writes.

## Resource cost and scheduling

| Class | Surfaces | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| low | CLI oracle, `cargo test` (warm), `gh api`, `sqlite3`, agent-browser idle | run freely; cargo waits on the shared lock if a build is in flight |
| medium | `trunk serve` with up to 3 agent-browser sessions (1.5 GB each upper bound), a live Droid session | one trunk on 3141; close sessions when done |
| high | `cargo llvm-cov` (load 3.3 to 14.6), first `cargo tauri dev` build, cold `trunk serve` build (7 rustc at 40-99 % CPU, largest 727 MB) | alone; nothing else compiling; validators wait for builds to finish |

Sample resources with `ps -axo pid,ppid,rss,%cpu,command | grep -E 'trunk|rustc --crate-name|cargo|agent-browser|remote-debugging-port'`,
`sysctl -n vm.loadavg`, `memory_pressure | tail -3`. Paste numbers into findings; do not estimate.

## Isolation

- One `trunk serve` on 3141 serves every validator; browser state is isolated per `--session <name>`.
  A second trunk (another worktree, a release build) goes to a scratch port 3142-3149.
- Config overrides go through a temp file: write `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current/target/scratch/<name>/config.toml`
  (copy of `config/observatory.example.toml` with the changed keys, including `[store].path` pointing into the
  same scratch dir) and run the CLI or app with `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<that path>`. Never edit
  `~/.droid-observatory/config.toml` or the owner's store.
- Scratch directories live under the worktree's `target/scratch/` (ignored by git through `target/`); nothing
  under `/home/user/.factory/sessions/` or another worktree.
- Screenshots and logs go to `/tmp/observatory-*` and are referenced by path and byte size in the report.
- Keychain values are never printed; `security find-generic-password -s <service>` without `-w` is the only
  allowed keychain command.

## Owner screenshot at integration

At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot of the Tauri window with the display
unlocked and attaches it to the boundary report (`reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` or the usage report
references the path). Validators do not block on this: their smoke evidence stands on its own, and the
integration feature records the screenshot path.

## Runtime findings (to be filled by validators)

- S: window title and lane names observed; `unknown events: N` of the S fixture.
- M0: store tables, `inspect` sample pointer, role resolution results.
- M1: file-picker steps, tray count vs `unknown events`, attach latency numbers, scrubber behaviour.
- M2: host launch flags, JSON-RPC method names, reaping evidence.
- M3: stall flag timing against `[intervention].stall_threshold_min` (20).
- M4: run ids, PR numbers, 403 surface text with the read-only token.
- M5: oracle diff summary, Grafana series count and labels, telemetry-off UI text.

# Droid session files

**What belongs here:** everything known about the files Droid 0.247.0 writes under `~/.factory/sessions/`,
which `mapping::v1` reads (planning note 1, dependency readiness report, architecture §4-§5), plus the
fixture layout and header. Facts are from the readiness report or from a keys-only inspection of this
mission's own session directory at drafting time (2026-10-22, 24 `.jsonl`); values were not read except
tag names, model ids, tool names and `subagent_type`. Items marked "M0 to confirm" are frozen by the M0
mapping worker in the decision file.

**What does not belong here:** the mapping table itself (architecture §5 and `mapping/v1/kinds.rs`), Rust
conventions, environment facts other than the directory path.

## Directory and file set

- Directory: `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/` where the slug is the working directory with `/` replaced by
  `-`: `~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/`.
- Flat: no subdirectories. Child sessions are sibling files.
- Per session `<session-id>` (UUID): `<id>.jsonl` (the transcript), `<id>.settings.json` (the sidecar),
  `<id>.settings.json.bak`. Counts at drafting: 72 entries = 24 of each. The readiness report saw 12, then
  14 `.jsonl`.
- There is no Droid version anywhere in these files. The mapping version is selected from `droid_version` in
  the fixture header (`0.247.*` maps to `V1`; anything else gives `LATEST` with
  `Warning::UnknownDroidVersion`); a live attach records `droid --version` into the `captures` row.
- The directory is read-only for the mission. Fixtures are byte-identical copies.

## JSONL line types

`type` values and counts over the 24 files at drafting:

```text
3890 message
  54 agent_turn_outcome
  37 todo_state
  24 session_start
   5 compaction_state
```

### `session_start` (first line of each file)

Keys observed (two shapes):

```text
["callingSessionId","callingToolUseId","cwd","hostId","id","isSessionTitleManuallySet","organizationId","owner","title","type","version"]   child
["cwd","hostId","id","isSessionTitleManuallySet","organizationId","owner","sessionTitleAutoStage","title","type","version"]                root
```

- `version` is the numeric schema version: `2` on all 24 files. It is not the Droid version.
- `callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId` are the parent linkage: a file whose `callingSessionId` equals a
  known session id is a child; the root has none. At drafting: 2 roots, 22 children. The root `id` is the
  mission id used by the mapper (`mission_id` = root session id).
- `callingToolUseId` matches the `id` of a `tool_use` part (tool `Task`) in the parent's transcript; the two id
  styles seen are `toolu_bdrk_...` and `call_...`.

### `message`

Top-level keys: `id, message, parentId, seq, timestamp, type` (3601 lines); 265 lines add
`compactionSummaryId`; the 24 first messages have no `parentId`. `timestamp` is RFC 3339.

`message` object keys:

- user: `content, role, visibility` and often `userMessageSource`.
- assistant: `apiProvider, content, modelId, reasoningEffort, role` (211 lines carry these three model keys).
  `modelId` values at drafting: `claude-fable-5.1` (369), `gpt-6.1-sol` (23), `gpt-6-sol` (15).
  A change of `modelId` between consecutive assistant messages of one session is `ModelChanged`.

`content[]` part `type` counts: `tool_use` 1661, `tool_result` 1659, `text` 410, `thinking` 263.
`tool_use` parts: `{id, name, input}`; `tool_result`: `{tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`.
Tool names seen (architecture §5): `Task`, `Execute`, `Script`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Create`, `Grep`, `Glob`,
`LS`, `TodoWrite`, `AskUser`, `ProposeMission`, `Skill`, `FetchUrl`, `WaitForScript`, `ApplyPatch`.

`Task` input keys observed: `await, complexity, description, prompt, subagent_type` (16), without
`complexity` (4), without `await` (2). `subagent_type` values: `worker` (20), `explorer` (2). No validator
spawn exists yet in this directory; the exact `subagent_type` strings for the scrutiny and user-testing
validators are **M0 to confirm** from the S capture.

### `agent_turn_outcome`

Keys `reason, resultKind, turnId, type`. `resultKind` values: `text` (42), `null` (12). In a child session it
maps to `TaskDone`, then `SubagentFinished` at EOF.

### `todo_state`

Keys `id, messageIndex, timestamp, todos, type`. Maps to `PlanRevised` when the todos changed.

### `compaction_state`

Keys `anchorMessage, id, loadedDeferredToolNames, removedCount, retainedImages, retainedSkills, summaryKind,
summaryText, summaryTokens, systemInfo, systemInfoText, timestamp, type`. Maps to `ContextCompacted`.
`summaryText` is free text and is never logged or exported.

## Sidecar `<id>.settings.json`

Keys present on all 24 files: `tokenUsage, inclusiveTokenUsage, lastCallTokenUsage,
childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId, assistantActiveTimeMs, model, reasoningEffort, interactionMode,
autonomyLevel, autonomyMode, toolExecutionMode, toolExecutionModeModelId, providerLock, providerLockTimestamp,
apiProviderLock, compactionThresholdCheckEnabled, allowSubagentsInScripts`. On most: `tags` (23),
`systemPrompt` (22), `disabledToolIds` (22); on a few: `enabledToolIds` (3), `artifacts` (3).

- `tokenUsage` keys: `inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens, thinkingTokens,
  factoryCredits`. The same shape for `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage` and each value of
  `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId` (keyed by child session id). This is where usage lives: there are
  no `usage.reported` lines in the JSONL. The mapper emits `UsageReported` from it once at EOF or when it
  changes.
- `model` values at drafting: `claude-fable-5.1` (19), `gpt-6.1-sol` (5). Model = assistant `modelId`, else
  sidecar `model`.
- `tags` is an array of objects `{ "name": <string>, "metadata": <object|null> }`, not an array of strings.
  Shapes observed:

  ```text
  { "name": "mission-session", "metadata": { "role": "orchestrator", "missionId": "<mission dir id>" } }   1 (the orchestrator)
  { "name": "subagent",        "metadata": { "callingSessionId": "<id>", "callingToolUseId": "<id>" } }  20
  { "name": "read-only",       "metadata": null }                                                       2
  ```

  `missionId` equals the Factory mission directory id (`~/.factory/missions/<missionId>`). Architecture §5
  step (3) of role resolution describes a `role:<x>` tag entry; the real shape is `metadata.role` on the
  `mission-session` tag, present only for the orchestrator so far. **M0 to confirm** whether workers and
  validators get a `role` in their tags and whether `droid exec --tag` values appear here or elsewhere.
- `systemPrompt` is never logged or stored. Unknown keys are ignored by `ingest::sidecar`.

## Ids and roles: what is known and what M0 confirms

| Need | Source today | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `mission_id` | root session id (`session_start.id` with no `callingSessionId`); cross-check `tags[].metadata.missionId` | known |
| parent / child | `session_start.callingSessionId`, `callingToolUseId`; `tags[name=subagent].metadata` repeats both | known |
| role | (1) no `callingSessionId` = orchestrator; (2) parent's `Task` part with `id == callingToolUseId`: `input.subagent_type` (`worker` seen); (3) `tags[].metadata.role`; (4) `Unresolved` | validator strings M0 to confirm |
| `milestone_id`, `feature_id` | `Task` input `description`/`prompt` matched against the `ProposeMission` plan | exact fields M0 to confirm |
| `--tag` values | not observed in this directory | M0 to confirm (where they land, if at all) |
| Droid version | absent from all files | fixture header / `droid --version` at attach |

**What belongs here:** the workflows and their jobs, the aggregate check names, the rulesets, how to read run
results and measure wall time, and the git rules every agent obeys. Sources: `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
`docs/decisions/D-003`, `D-007`, `SPEC.md` §7, `architecture.md` §15, session log entry 25.

**What does not belong here:** the integration procedure and the reports written at a boundary
(`integration-and-boundaries.md`), token and keychain facts beyond what the gate lane needs (`environment.md`).

Repository: `dctellya/droid-observatory`. Default branch `main`. Mission branch `mission/observatory-v1`
(from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`). Every action is pinned to a commit digest with a
version comment (Renovate keeps them current, D-005).

## `mission-branch.yml`

Triggers: `push` and `pull_request` on `mission/**`, `workflow_call`, `workflow_dispatch`. Permissions
`contents: read`. Concurrency group per ref with `cancel-in-progress: true`. Env: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`,
`RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`. Budget: 3 minutes warm (rule 6).

| Job | Timeout | Gated by | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `detect` | 2 | always | outputs `has_rust` (`Cargo.toml` exists), `has_fixtures` (`fixtures/streams/*.jsonl`) |
| `docs` | 5 | always | markdownlint-cli2 on `**/*.md`, `make check-decisions-index`, `make check-file-size`, `make check-todos` |
| `links` | 5 | always | lychee `--config lychee.toml "**/*.md"`, fail on broken |
| `workflows` | 3 | always | actionlint 1.7.12 |
| `secrets` | 5 | always | gitleaks-action over the full history (`fetch-depth: 0`) |
| `rust` | 15 | `has_rust` | dtolnay/rust-toolchain (version from `rust-toolchain.toml`), rust-cache, `make fmt-check`, `make lint`, `make test`, `make replay-fixtures` (if `has_fixtures`) |
| `deny` | 5 | `has_rust` | cargo-deny-action `check --all-features` |
| `machete` (added in S, B-014) | 5 | `has_rust` | taiki-e/install-action `cargo-machete@0.9.2`, `cargo machete` |
| `coverage` (added in S, B-005) | 15 | `has_rust` | rust-toolchain with `llvm-tools-preview`, rust-cache, `cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1`, `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --all-features --fail-under-lines ${{ env.COVERAGE_MIN }} --summary-only`; `COVERAGE_MIN: "0"` in S, `"80"` from the M0 integration |
| `mission-checks` | 1 | `if: always()` | aggregate: `needs: [detect, docs, links, workflows, secrets, rust, deny]` (+ `machete`, `coverage` from S); fails on any `failure` or `cancelled` in `needs`; skipped jobs count as not applicable |

`mission-checks` is the single name other tooling depends on; new jobs are appended to its `needs`, never to
the ruleset. If the warm time exceeds 3 min after `coverage` joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
decision file (SPEC §7).

Trigger: `pull_request` to `main` (and `workflow_dispatch`). Jobs: `detect` (adds `has_tauri` from
`apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`), `light` (reuses `mission-branch.yml`, so machete and
coverage join it automatically), `sast` (semgrep 1.182.0 container: `p/default p/rust p/secrets
p/github-actions`, SARIF artifact), `sast-upload` (codeql-action upload-sarif, category `semgrep`), `fs-scan`
(trivy fs: vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH, CRITICAL; SARIF uploaded), `workflow-policy` (checkov on
`.github/workflows`), `sbom` (anchore sbom-action, spdx-json), `bundle` (if `has_tauri`, calls
`bundle.yml`), and the aggregate **`gate`** (`needs: [detect, light, sast, sast-upload, fs-scan,
workflow-policy, sbom, bundle]`, `if: always()`, fails on `failure`/`cancelled`). `gate` is the only status
check the `main-gate` ruleset requires (D-003, D-007). Measured on PR #23 (no Rust yet): wall time
9 min 19 s (`created 2026-10-22T14:31:43Z`, `updated 14:41:02Z`), the `gate` job itself 4 s; jobs: detect 3s,
workflow-policy 20s, sast 23s, sast-upload 13s, sbom 11s, fs-scan 22s, light / docs 6s, light / links 4s,
light / secrets 16s, light / workflows 7s, light / mission-checks 4s.

## `bundle.yml`

Reusable (`workflow_call`), `macos-latest`, timeout 45, permissions `contents: read`, `id-token: write`,
`attestations: write`. Steps: rust-toolchain, rust-cache, `taiki-e/install-action` with `tool: trunk,tauri-cli`

`bundle-macos`. Note the `target/` paths: CI has no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` override.

Trigger: tags `v*`. `verify` (tag commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`; tag matches

```yaml

on: { pull_request: { branches: [demo/base], types: [opened, synchronize, labeled, unlabeled] } }

      - run: |

            echo "label demo:red present: red by design"; exit 1; fi

```

- `main-gate`: id `25636994`, enforcement active, target `refs/heads/main`: pull request required with 0
  approving reviews, required status check `gate` (strict), deletion and non-fast-forward blocked, no bypass
  actors (admins included). Off-limits for the mission.
- `demo-gate` (M4, B-007): to be created on `refs/heads/demo/base` with `gh api` by the orchestrator (the
  owner does it if the token lacks admin). Read the existing one first and mirror its shape:

  ```sh
  gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/rulesets
  gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/rulesets/25636994
  gh api -X POST repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/rulesets --input demo-gate-ruleset.json   # M4 writes the JSON from the main-gate shape: name demo-gate, target branch, include refs/heads/demo/base, rules pull_request + required_status_checks context demo-gate
  ```

  Exact payload: **M4 to confirm** against the API response of `main-gate`.

## Reading run results

```sh
gh run list --branch mission/observatory-v1 --workflow mission-branch --limit 10 \
  --json databaseId,status,conclusion,headSha,createdAt,updatedAt,displayTitle
gh run view <run-id>                                   # per-job durations
gh run view <run-id> --json createdAt,updatedAt,conclusion,jobs
gh run view <run-id> --log-failed
gh run watch <run-id>                                  # blocks until done
gh api "repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>" --jq '.workflow_runs[] | {id, name, status, conclusion, created_at, updated_at}'
gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/commits/<sha>/status --jq '{state, statuses: [.statuses[] | {context, state}]}'
gh pr checks <n> --watch=false
gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup
```

The read-only PAT in the keychain has Actions and Commit statuses read; it cannot call the check-runs API
(no Checks permission). The owner's `gh` login (`dctellya`, admin) can.

## Wall time for `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md`

Measured, never estimated (rule 7, rule 11): take `createdAt` and `updatedAt` of the `mission-branch` run on
the integration push (`gh run view <id> --json createdAt,updatedAt,conclusion`), paste both timestamps and
the difference, the run URL `https://github.com/dctellya/droid-observatory/actions/runs/<id>`, and the per-job
durations from `gh run view <id>`. Example from entry 25: run `39796410945`, created `2026-10-22T14:31:43Z`,
updated `14:41:02Z`, wall time 9 min 19 s. Compare against the 3-minute warm budget and say whether the run
was warm (rust-cache hit) or cold.

## Git rules (rule 12, hooks)

- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single PR, opened by the orchestrator after M5, merged by the
  owner when `gate` is green. Direct pushes to `main` are refused by `.githooks/pre-push`, by
  `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` (exit 2) and by the ruleset.
- Forward only: `guard-git.sh` blocks `commit --amend`, `reset --hard|--soft|--mixed`, `rebase`, `stash`,
  `push --force|-f|+ref`, and committing on `main`. `pre-push` refuses any non-fast-forward. Fix with a new
  commit; never `--no-verify`.
- Pushes allowed: `mission/**`, `wt/**`, `demo/**` branches. One outward write besides pushes: the M4 demo
  merge (performed by the owner) and the `demo/base` ruleset, branch and label setup with `gh`.
- `commit-msg`: subject non-empty, at most 72 characters, no `WIP`/`fixup!`/`squash!`. Co-author trailer on
  agent commits: `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.
- `pre-commit`: gitleaks on staged files, file size (200 KB), debt markers, decisions index when a `D-` file is
  staged, rustfmt when `.rs` files are staged, markdownlint on staged `.md`.
- Each worktree is its own checkout but shares `.git/config`, so `core.hooksPath=.githooks` (set by
  `make hooks`) covers them; `init.sh` verifies the hook files and `.factory/hooks.json` are present.
- A hook that is missing is reported and the worker stops (`docs/runbooks/hooks-disabled.md`); it is never
  disabled or bypassed.

## Findings worth the parent's attention

1. **Tauri/trunk coexistence**: the task text says tauri-dev "reuses a running trunk on 3141 or starts its own". The readiness report says the opposite: `cargo tauri dev` always starts its own trunk through `beforeDevCommand`, and a standalone trunk already on 3141 makes that second trunk fail to bind. I documented the measured behaviour (stop `trunk-ui` first; the trunk started by `tauri-dev` then serves agent-browser on 3141, which was verified) rather than the "reuse" wording.
2. **`tags` shape in `.settings.json`** (observed at drafting, 24 files): `tags` is an array of objects `{ "name", "metadata" }`, not strings. Shapes: `mission-session` with `metadata.role = "orchestrator"` and `metadata.missionId` (equal to the mission directory id), `subagent` with `metadata.callingSessionId`/`callingToolUseId`, `read-only` with `metadata: null`. Architecture §5 role-resolution step (3) assumes a `role:<x>` string tag; `droid-sessions.md` records the real shape and marks it "M0 to confirm".
3. **Validator spawns**: `subagent_type` values seen so far are only `worker` (20) and `explorer` (2); the scrutiny/user-testing strings are marked "M0 to confirm".
4. **Listening ports at drafting**: 5000 and 7000 are held by `ControlCe` (Control Center), 8000 by `surreal`, 11434 by `ollama`, 18444/18446/18450/18451 by `probe`/`probe2`/`showroom`. Docker was not visible in the TCP listener list; it is listed as off-limits on the parent's word.
5. **`.env.example` vs reality**: the example still describes a `pull_requests:write, checks:read` token; the keychain item is read-only. Noted in `environment.md`; the file itself is the repository's to fix at a later integration.
